title.en: Volume 467 Biographies 226: Eunuchs 2 - Yang Shouzhen, Han Shouying, Lan Jizong, Zhangwei Jiyang's son: Ruo Shui, Gan Zhaoji, Lu Shouqin, Wang Shougui, Li Xian, Zhang Maoze, Song Yongchen, Wang Zhongzheng, Li Shunju, Shi Deyi, Liang Congji, Liu Weijian
title.raw: 卷四百六十七 列傳第二百二十六 宦者二 楊守珍 韓守英 藍繼宗 張惟吉養子:若水 甘昭吉 盧守懃 王守規 李憲 張茂則 宋用臣 王中正 李舜舉 石得一 梁從吉 劉惟簡 Volume 467 Biographies 226: Eunuchs 2 - Yang Shouzhen, Han Shouying, Lan Jizong, Zhangwei Jiyang's son: Ruo Shui, Gan Zhaoji, Lu Shouqin, Wang Shougui, Li Xian, Zhang Maoze, Song Yongchen, Wang Zhongzheng, Li Shunju, Shi Deyi, Liang Congji, Liu Weijian

sentences.zh: 宦者二

translations.literal: Eunuchs, Part Two
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs II

sentences.zh: ○楊守珍韓守英藍繼宗張惟吉甘昭吉盧守勤王守規李憲張茂則宋用臣王中正李舜舉石得一梁從吉劉惟簡

translations.literal: ○ Yang Shouzhen, Han Shouying, Lan Jizong, Zhang Wei Ji, Gan Zhaoji, Lu Shouqin, Wang Shougui, Li Xian, Zhang Maozi, Song Yongchen, Wang Zhongzheng, Li Shunju, Shi Deyi, Liang Congji, Liu Weijian
translations.idiomatic: ○ Yang Shouzhen · Han Shouying · Lan Jizong · Zhang Wei Ji · Gan Zhaoji · Lu Shouqin · Wang Shougui · Li Xian · Zhang Maozi · Song Yongchen · Wang Zhongzheng · Li Shunju · Shi Deyi · Liang Congji · Liu Weijian

sentences.zh: 楊守珍，字仲寶，開 封祥符人。

translations.literal: Yang Shouzhen, courtesy name Zhongbao, was a native of Xiangfu in Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shouzhen (courtesy name Zhongbao) came from Xiangfu in Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 為入內黃門，習書史，學兵家方略。

translations.literal: He became an Inner Yellow Gate attendant, studied histories, and learned military strategists' methods.
translations.idiomatic: Entering palace service as an Inner Yellow Gate attendant, he studied historiography and military strategy.

sentences.zh: 善射，家僮過堂下，一發貫髻，人服其精。

translations.literal: Skilled at archery; when a household servant passed beneath the hall, one shot pierced his hair-knot, and people admired his precision.
translations.idiomatic: A fine archer, he once pierced a servant's topknot with a single arrow as the man crossed the hall below—an exploit that won universal admiration.

sentences.zh: 選為環慶路走馬承受公事。

translations.literal: Selected as courier commissioner for Huanqing Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was chosen to serve as the Huanqing Circuit courier commissioner.

sentences.zh: 契丹謀入塞，為鎮、定、高陽關行營同押先鋒 事。

translations.literal: When the Khitan plotted to invade the frontier, he served as joint vanguard commander for the mobile camp at Zhen, Ding, and Gaoyang Pass.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan threatened a border incursion, he was named joint vanguard commander of the mobile headquarters covering Zhen, Ding, and Gaoyang Pass.

sentences.zh: 會許民周繼宗為人誣告與外夷交通，幹證者六十人，辭服，遣守珍覆問，悉辦理出之。

translations.literal: It happened that the commoner Zhou Jizong of Xu was falsely accused of dealings with foreign tribes; sixty corroborating witnesses testified, and their statements held. Shouzhen was sent to reinvestigate and fully cleared all who had been implicated.
translations.idiomatic: A man of Xu named Zhou Jizong had been falsely accused of trafficking with foreign tribes; sixty witnesses' testimony seemed to convict him. Dispatched to re-examine the case, Shouzhen established the truth and secured the release of every person implicated.

sentences.zh: 徙真定、保、趙等州駐泊都監，邕、桂等十州安撫都監。

translations.literal: Transferred to garrison commandant at Zhending, Ba, and Zhao among other prefectures, and pacification commandant for ten prefectures including Yong and Gui.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to garrison commandant at Zhending, Ba, Zhao, and related prefectures, and pacification commandant over Yong, Gui, and eight other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 從曹克明降撫水 州蠻，築二柵以扼其要。

translations.literal: Following Cao Keming, he subdued and soothed the Shui prefecture barbarians and built two stockades to command the key points.
translations.idiomatic: Serving under Cao Keming, he helped pacify the tribes of Shui Prefecture and built two stockades to hold the strategic passes.

sentences.zh: 天禧初，擒盜於青灰山。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tianxi era, he captured bandits at Qinghui Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianxi reign, he captured bandits on Qinghui Mountain.

sentences.zh: 累遷西京作坊使、帶禦器械、永興軍兵馬鈐轄，徙真定、邠寧路。

translations.literal: Repeatedly promoted to Western Capital Workshop Commissioner, Bearer of Imperial Apparatus, military commander at Yongxing Army; transferred to Zhending and Binning circuits.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through West Capital workshop commissioner, bearer of imperial arms, and Yongxing Army military commander, then was posted to Zhending and Binning circuits.

sentences.zh: 為內侍省內侍押班，提點內弓箭軍器庫。

translations.literal: Became Inner Attendant Service chamberlain escort leader and overseer of the Inner Bow and Weapon Depots.
translations.idiomatic: He became chief escort of the Inner Attendant Service and superintendent of the inner bow and weapons arsenals.

sentences.zh: 進內園 使、右班都知、領端州刺史。

translations.literal: Advanced to Inner Garden Commissioner, Right Bureau Director, and acting prefect of Duanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Inner Garden commissioner, director of the right bureau, and nominal prefect of Duanzhou.

sentences.zh: 嚐侍仁宗苑中，命乘馬馳射，賞其便習，賜錦袍卮酒。

translations.literal: Once attending Emperor Renzong in the imperial park, he was ordered to gallop and shoot from horseback; the Emperor admired his ease and rewarded him with a brocade robe and a cup of wine.
translations.idiomatic: While attending Renzong in the imperial park, he was told to ride and shoot at the gallop; pleased with his skill, the emperor gave him a brocade robe and wine.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈原州防禦使。

translations.literal: On his death he was posthumously made Defender of Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously honored as defender-general of Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 韓守英，字德華，開封祥符人。

translations.literal: Han Shouying, courtesy name Dehua, was a native of Xiangfu in Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Han Shouying (courtesy name Dehua) came from Xiangfu in Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 初為入內高 品，從征河東，數奉詔至石嶺關督戰，取隆州，遷殿頭。

translations.literal: At first an Inner Attendant senior rank; he followed the eastern campaign, repeatedly received edicts to supervise fighting at Shiling Pass, captured Long prefecture, and was promoted to Hall Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a senior-ranked Inner Attendant, joined the eastern campaign, was repeatedly ordered to direct fighting at Shiling Pass, took Long Prefecture, and was promoted to hall chief.

sentences.zh: 久之，以西頭供奉官擢入內內侍押班，遷副都知。

translations.literal: After a long time, from Western Head Palace Attendant he was raised to Inner Attendant Service chief escort and promoted to deputy director.
translations.idiomatic: Years later he was elevated from Western Head palace attendant to chief escort of the Inner Attendant Service, then to deputy director.

sentences.zh: 隨王繼恩招安西川，為先鋒，戰於劍門有功，遷西京作坊 使、劍門都監。

translations.literal: Following Wang Jien in pacifying Chuan, he served as vanguard; fighting at Jianmen he had merit and was promoted to Western Capital Workshop Commissioner and Jianmen garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Wang Jien in the pacification of Sichuan as vanguard commander; his victory at Jianmen won him promotion to West Capital workshop commissioner and commandant of Jianmen.

sentences.zh: 還，勾當三班院，進入內內侍都知。

translations.literal: On returning, he managed the Three-Rank Bureau and advanced to Inner Attendant Service director.
translations.idiomatic: After his return he oversaw the Three-Rank Bureau and was made director of the Inner Attendant Service.

sentences.zh: 曆定州、鎮定高陽關、並代路兵馬鈐轄。

translations.literal: He successively served as military commander of Dingzhou, Zhending-Gaoyang Pass, and Hedong circuits.
translations.idiomatic: He held successive posts as military commander on the Dingzhou, Zhending–Gaoyang Pass, and Hedong circuits.

sentences.zh: 契丹圍岢嵐軍，守英與鈐轄張誌言、知府州折惟昌帥所部渡河，抵朔 州，以牽賊勢。

translations.literal: When the Khitan besieged Kelan Army, Shouying with military commander Zhang Zhiyan and Yong prefecture magistrate Zhe Weichang led their troops across the river as far as Shuozhou to draw off the enemy's strength.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan besieged Kelan Army, Shouying joined Zhang Zhiyan, circuit commander, and Zhe Weichang, prefect of Yong, in crossing the Yellow River with their forces as far as Shuozhou to distract the enemy.

sentences.zh: 遂破狼水砦，俘數百人，獲馬牛羊鎧甲以數萬計，賊為解去。

translations.literal: Thereupon they smashed Langshui Stockade, captured several hundred men, and took horses, cattle, sheep, and armor by the tens of thousands; the bandits thereby lifted the siege.
translations.idiomatic: They stormed Langshui stockade, took several hundred prisoners, and seized tens of thousands of head of livestock and suits of armor, whereupon the Khitan broke off the siege.

sentences.zh: 賜錦袍、金帶。

translations.literal: He was given a brocade robe and gold belt.
translations.idiomatic: The court rewarded him with a brocade robe and gold belt.

sentences.zh: 俄領會州刺史，解都知。

translations.literal: Shortly he acted as prefect of Huizhou and was relieved of the directorship.
translations.idiomatic: He soon received the nominal prefecture of Huizhou and resigned the directorship.

sentences.zh: 再遷昭宣使，復領三班。

translations.literal: Again promoted to Zhaoxuan Commissioner and again placed over the Three-Rank Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to Zhaoxuan commissioner and once more placed in charge of the Three-Rank Bureau.

sentences.zh: 出為鄜延路都鈐轄，徙並代路。

translations.literal: Sent out as military commander of Fuyan Circuit and transferred to Hedong Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as military commander of Fuyan Circuit, then transferred to Hedong.

sentences.zh: 建言：“本路宿兵多，百姓困於飛挽，今幸邊鄙無事，請留騎軍千，餘人悉徙內地。”

translations.literal: He submitted a proposal: "This circuit has many garrison troops; the people are exhausted by emergency transport. Now that fortunately the border is quiet, I ask to retain a thousand cavalry and move all the rest to the interior."
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "This circuit keeps too many troops on station; the people are ground down supplying them by forced transport. The frontier is quiet for now—let a thousand cavalry remain and send the rest inland."

sentences.zh: 真宗曰：“邊臣能體朝廷恤民之意，宜詔諸路視此行之。”

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong said: "A frontier official who can embody the court's care for the people deserves an edict that every circuit follow this example."
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong replied: "When a border commander grasps the court's wish to spare the people, every circuit should be ordered to do the same.

sentences.zh: 提舉在京諸司庫務，勾當皇城司，為趙德明官告使。

translations.literal: Superintendent of capital bureau storehouses, manager of the Imperial City Office, and envoy bearing patent office for Zhao Deming.
translations.idiomatic: He superintended capital bureau storehouses, managed the Imperial City Office, and served as patent envoy to Zhao Deming.

sentences.zh: 曆宣政、宣慶二使，內侍左班都知，領獎州團練使、雅州防禦使，入內都知，管勾修國史。

translations.literal: Successively Xuanzheng and Xuanqing commissioners, Left Bureau director of Inner Attendants, acting Jiang regiment commander and Ya prefecture defender-general, Inner Service director, and overseer of compilation of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: He held the Xuanzheng and Xuanqing commissions in turn, directed the left bureau of the Inner Attendant Service, served as nominal Jiang regiment commander and Ya defender-general, became Inner Service director, and oversaw compilation of the national history.

sentences.zh: 書成，進景福殿使，又為延福宮使、入內都知，復提舉諸司庫務。

translations.literal: When the book was completed, he was advanced to Jingfu Hall Commissioner; again made Yanfu Palace commissioner and Inner Service director, and again superintendent of capital bureau storehouses.
translations.idiomatic: When the history was finished he was made Jingfu Hall commissioner; he later served again as Yanfu Palace commissioner and Inner Service director and once more superintended capital bureau storehouses.

sentences.zh: 卒贈定國軍節度觀察留後。

translations.literal: On death posthumously made Military Commissioner and Observation Commissioner of Dingguo Army.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously honored as military commissioner and observation commissioner of the Dingguo Army.

sentences.zh: 藍繼宗，字承祖，廣州南海人。

translations.literal: Lan Jizong, courtesy name Chengzu, was a native of Nanhai in Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lan Jizong (courtesy name Chengzu) was from Nanhai in Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 事劉鋹為宦者，歸朝，年十二，遷為中黃門。

translations.literal: He had served Liu Chang as a eunuch; after submitting to the dynasty, at age twelve he was promoted to Central Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He had been a eunuch in Liu Chang's court; after surrendering to the Song he was, at twelve, promoted to Central Yellow Gate attendant.

sentences.zh: 從征太原，傳詔營陳間，多稱旨。

translations.literal: He followed the Taiyuan campaign; transmitting edicts among the battle lines he often met approval.
translations.idiomatic: On the Taiyuan campaign he carried edicts along the fighting front and repeatedly won imperial praise.

sentences.zh: 秦州並邊有大、小洛門砦，自唐末陷西羌。

translations.literal: Along Qin prefecture's border with the west were the Great and Small Luomen stockades, lost to the Western Qiang since late Tang.
translations.idiomatic: On the Qinzhou frontier lay the Great and Small Luomen stockades, held by Western Qiang tribes since late Tang.

sentences.zh: 雍熙中，溫仲舒諭酋豪使獻其地，徒眾渭北。

translations.literal: In the Yongxi era, Wen Zhongshu persuaded the chieftains to offer the land and move their people north of the Wei.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongxi, Wen Zhongshu persuaded the tribal chiefs to surrender the stockades and resettle their followers north of the Wei River.

sentences.zh: 言者以為生事，請罷仲舒。

translations.literal: Critics held that this stirred trouble and asked that Zhongshu be removed.
translations.idiomatic: Critics called it needless provocation and demanded Zhongshu's recall.

sentences.zh: 太宗遣繼宗往按視，還奏二砦據要害，產良木，不可棄。

translations.literal: Taizong sent Jizong to inspect on the spot; on return he reported that the two stockades commanded vital ground and produced fine timber and could not be abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong dispatched Jizong to inspect in person; he reported that both stockades occupied vital ground, yielded excellent timber, and must be kept.

sentences.zh: 帝悅，復使繼宗勞賜仲舒。

translations.literal: The Emperor was pleased and again sent Jizong to console Zhongshu with rewards.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and sent Jizong back to Zhongshu with gifts and commendation.

sentences.zh: 累遷西京作坊副使、勾當內東門。

translations.literal: Repeatedly promoted to deputy Western Capital workshop commissioner and manager of the Inner East Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through deputy West Capital workshop commissioner to manager of the Inner East Gate.

sentences.zh: 元德太后、章穆皇后葬，為按行園陵使。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Yuande and Empress Zhangmu were buried, he served as commissioner surveying the mausoleum route.
translations.idiomatic: At the burials of Empress Yuande and Empress Zhangmu he served as commissioner for surveying the tomb park.

sentences.zh: 車駕北征，勾當留司、皇城司。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage marched north, he managed the stay-behind offices and Imperial City Office.
translations.idiomatic: On the emperor's northern expedition he managed capital affairs left behind at court and the Imperial City Office.

sentences.zh: 車駕謁諸陵，近陵舊乏水，繼宗疏泉陵下，百司從官皆取以濟。

translations.literal: When the emperor visited the tombs, water had long been scarce near the mausoleums; Jizong opened springs beneath the tombs, and all following officials drew from them.
translations.idiomatic: On a tour of the imperial tombs, where water had long been scarce, Jizong tapped springs below the mounds so that the entire entourage could be supplied.

sentences.zh: 擢入內副都知，為天書扶 侍都監。

translations.literal: Raised to Inner Deputy Director and made Director of the Heavenly Book Escort.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to deputy director of the Inner Service and made director of the Heavenly Book escort corps.

sentences.zh: 詔與李神祐第東封扈從內臣之勞，而入內供奉官範守遜等訴其不公，罷都知。

translations.literal: An edict ranked with Li Shenyou the merit of inner attendants on the eastern pilgrimage; but Inner Palace Attendant Fan Shouyun and others complained of injustice, and he was removed as director.
translations.idiomatic: The court ranked his service on the eastern pilgrimage alongside Li Shenyou's, but Fan Shouyun and other inner attendants protested unfair ranking, and he lost the directorship.

sentences.zh: 祀汾脽，復為天書扶侍都監，再遷東染院使。

translations.literal: On offering sacrifice at Fen Hill, again made Director of the Heavenly Book Escort and again promoted to East Dye Yard Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: At the Fenzhou sacrifice he again headed the Heavenly Book escort and was promoted to East Dye Yard commissioner.

sentences.zh: 明年，領會州刺 史，進崇儀使、勾當皇城司。

translations.literal: Next year acting prefect of Huizhou, advanced to Chongyi Commissioner and manager of Imperial City Office.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he held Huizhou in name, was promoted to Chongyi commissioner, and managed the Imperial City Office.

sentences.zh: 修玉清昭應宮，與劉承珪典工作。

translations.literal: In repairing the Yuqing Zhaoying Palace he joined Liu Chenggui in directing the work.
translations.idiomatic: He and Liu Chenggui jointly directed construction of the Yuqing Zhaoying Palace.

sentences.zh: 宮成，遷洛苑使、高州團練使，充都監。

translations.literal: When the palace was finished, he was transferred to Luoyuan Commissioner and Gaozhou regiment commander, and made chief director.
translations.idiomatic: On completion he became Luoyuan commissioner and nominal Gaozhou regiment commander, serving as chief project director.

sentences.zh: 坐章穆皇后陵隧墊，貶如京使。

translations.literal: Punished for the subsidence of Empress Zhangmu's tomb passage, demoted to Rujing Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Zhangmu's tomb passage collapsed, he was demoted to Rujing commissioner.

sentences.zh: 典修景靈宮，進南作坊使， 復修會靈、祥源觀。

translations.literal: He directed repair of Jingling Palace, advanced to South Workshop Commissioner, and again repaired Huiling and Xiangyuan Shrines.
translations.idiomatic: He oversaw repairs at Jingling Palace, was promoted to South Workshop commissioner, and rebuilt the Huiling and Xiangyuan shrines.

sentences.zh: 車駕幸亳州，管勾留司、大內公事，提舉在京諸司庫務，勾當三班院，修國史院。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage visited Bozhou, he managed stay-behind capital affairs and inner palace business, superintended capital bureau storehouses, managed the Three-Rank Bureau, and repaired the History Institute.
translations.idiomatic: On the Bozhou tour he managed stay-behind court business and inner-palace affairs, superintended capital storehouses, oversaw the Three-Rank Bureau, and refurbished the History Institute.

sentences.zh: 為趙德明加恩使，德明與繼宗射，繼宗每發必中，德明遺以所 乘名馬。

translations.literal: Envoy to invest Zhao Deming with grace; Deming shot with Jizong, and Jizong hit with every shot; Deming presented his famous horse.
translations.idiomatic: As envoy to invest Zhao Deming with honors, he shot with Deming and never missed; Deming gave him his celebrated horse.

sentences.zh: 為內侍省右班都知，遷入內都知。

translations.literal: Became Right Bureau director of Inner Attendant Service and promoted to Inner Service director.
translations.idiomatic: He became right-bureau director of the Inner Attendant Service and then Inner Service director.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，遷左騏驥使、忠州防禦使、永定陵修奉鈐轄。

translations.literal: When Renzong took the throne, promoted to Left Imperial Stud Commissioner, Zhong prefecture defender-general, and repair superintendent at Yongding Tomb.
translations.idiomatic: At Renzong's accession he was made left imperial stud commissioner, nominal Zhong defender-general, and superintendent of Yongding Tomb repairs.

sentences.zh: 曆昭宣、宣政、宣慶使。

translations.literal: Successively Zhaoxuan, Xuanzheng, and Xuanqing commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: He held the Zhaoxuan, Xuanzheng, and Xuanqing commissions in succession.

sentences.zh: 累上章求致仕，特免入朝拜舞及從行幸。

translations.literal: Repeatedly memorialized requesting retirement; specially exempted from entering court to bow and from accompanying imperial tours.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly asked to retire and was specially excused from court bows and imperial progresses.

sentences.zh: 頃之，復固請罷都知，以景福殿使、邕州觀察使家居養疾。

translations.literal: Before long again firmly asked to resign the directorship; made Jingfu Hall Commissioner and Yongzhou observation commissioner to live at home and nurse illness.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he pressed again to resign the directorship and was allowed to keep Jingfu Hall commissioner and Yongzhou observation commissioner while recuperating at home.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈安德軍節度使，諡僖靖。

translations.literal: On death posthumously made Military Commissioner of Ande Army, posthumous name Xijing.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously made military commissioner of the Ande Army, with the posthumous epithet Xijing.

sentences.zh: 繼宗事四朝，謙謹自持，每領職未久，輒請罷。

translations.literal: Jizong served four reigns, holding himself with humility; each time he received an office not long he would ask to be relieved.
translations.idiomatic: Serving four reigns, Jizong kept to modest reserve; scarcely had he taken a post when he asked to be relieved of it.

sentences.zh: 家有園池，退朝即亟歸，同列或留之，繼宗曰：“我欲歸種花卉、弄遊魚為樂爾。”

translations.literal: He had a garden and pond; after court he would hurry home, and colleagues sometimes detained him—Jizong said, "I only wish to return and grow flowers and toy with fish for pleasure."
translations.idiomatic: He kept a garden pool at home and left court the moment he could; when colleagues tried to detain him he would say, "I only want to go home and tend my flowers and fish."

sentences.zh: 景福殿置使，自大中祥符間至繼宗，授者才三人。

translations.literal: The Jingfu Hall commission, from the Dazhong Xiangfu period to Jizong, had been conferred on only three men.
translations.idiomatic: From the Dazhong Xiangfu era until Jizong, only three men had ever received the Jingfu Hall commission.

sentences.zh: 養子元用、元震。

translations.literal: Adopted sons Yuanyong and Yuanzhen.
translations.idiomatic: His adopted sons were Yuanyong and Yuanzhen.

sentences.zh: 元用終左藏庫使、梓州觀察使。

translations.literal: Yuanyong ended as Left Treasury Commissioner and Zizhou observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyong rose to left treasury commissioner and nominal observation commissioner of Zizhou.

sentences.zh: 元震以兄蔭補入內黃門，轉高班，給事明肅太后。

translations.literal: Yuanzhen received office by his elder brother's privilege as Inner Yellow Gate, rose to Senior Rank, and attended Empress Dowager Mingsu.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhen entered service through his brother's privilege as Inner Yellow Gate attendant, rose to senior rank, and served Empress Dowager Mingsu.

sentences.zh: 禁中夜火，後擁仁宗登西華門，左右未集，元震獨傳呼宿衛，以功遷高品。

translations.literal: At night a fire broke out in the palace; the empress escorted Renzong up the West Huaming Gate; those left and right were not yet assembled—Yuanzhen alone called out the night guard, and for this merit was promoted to Senior Rank.
translations.idiomatic: When fire broke out in the palace at night, the empress hurried Renzong to the West Huaming Gate before the guard had gathered; Yuanzhen alone roused the night watch and was promoted for it.

sentences.zh: 為三陵都監，條列防守法，其後諸陵 以為式。

translations.literal: Made superintendent of the three imperial tombs and drew up rules for their defense; later tombs took this as model.
translations.idiomatic: As superintendent of the three imperial tomb precincts he drafted defensive regulations later adopted as the standard.

sentences.zh: 曆群牧都監，監三館秘閣，積官皇城使。

translations.literal: Successively herd commissioner, superintendent of the Three Institutes and Inner Archive, and accumulated office to Imperial City Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as herd commissioner and superintendent of the Three Institutes and secret archive, accumulating rank until imperial city commissioner.

sentences.zh: 累遷入內副都知、忠州防禦使。

translations.literal: Repeatedly promoted to Inner Deputy Director and Zhong prefecture defender-general.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to deputy director of the Inner Service and nominal defender-general of Zhong.

sentences.zh: 仙韶院火，元震救護，火以時息。

translations.literal: Fire at Xianyao Hall; Yuanzhen rescued and protected, and the fire was stopped in time.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianyao Hall caught fire, Yuanzhen led the rescue and the blaze was brought under control.

sentences.zh: 詔褒之，賜襲衣、金帶。

translations.literal: Edict praised him; given ceremonial dress and gold belt.
translations.idiomatic: An edict commended him and granted ceremonial robes and a gold belt.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈鎮海軍留後。

translations.literal: On death posthumously made Zhenhai Army deputy commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously made deputy commissioner of the Zhenhai Army.

sentences.zh: 元 震養子五人，不畜閹子。

translations.literal: Yuanzhen adopted five sons and did not keep castrated sons.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhen adopted five sons and refused to rear castrated heirs of his own.

sentences.zh: 張惟吉，字佑之，開封人。

translations.literal: Zhang Wei Ji, courtesy name Youzhi, was a native of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wei Ji (courtesy name Youzhi) was from Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 初補入內黃門，遷殿頭、高陽關路走馬承受公事。

translations.literal: At first supplemented as Inner Yellow Gate, promoted to Hall Chief and Gaoyang Pass courier commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as Inner Yellow Gate attendant, became hall chief, and served as Gaoyang Pass courier commissioner.

sentences.zh: 護塞滑州天台埽役，遷西頭供奉官，監在京榷貨 務。

translations.literal: Guarded the frontier embankment works at Huatai Mound in Huazhou, promoted to Western Head Palace Attendant and superintendent of the capital monopoly trade office.
translations.idiomatic: He supervised dike repairs at Huatai Mound in Huazhou, was promoted to Western Head palace attendant, and superintended the capital monopoly bureau.

sentences.zh: 知嘉州張約以贓敗，詔與御史王軫往劾其獄。

translations.literal: Jia prefecture magistrate Zhang Yue was ruined by bribery; an edict sent him with Censor Wang Zhen to investigate the case.
translations.idiomatic: When Jia prefect Zhang Yue fell to corruption charges, he and Censor Wang Zhen were ordered to conduct the investigation.

sentences.zh: 還，領內東門司，為修奉章獻、章懿太后二陵承受。

translations.literal: On return, he took charge of the Inner East Gate Office and served as commissioner for repairs to the tombs of Empresses Zhangxian and Zhangyi.
translations.idiomatic: Returning, he headed the Inner East Gate Office and oversaw repairs at the tombs of Empresses Zhangxian and Zhangyi.

sentences.zh: 時議復用李諮榷茶算緡法，乃以惟吉為內殿崇班，復監榷貨 務。

translations.literal: At the time it was debated to restore Li Zi's tea monopoly counting-cash law; he was made Inner Hall Honored Class and again superintendent of the monopoly trade office.
translations.idiomatic: When the court debated reviving Li Zi's tea monopoly surtax, he was made Inner Hall honored-class attendant and again placed over the monopoly bureau.

sentences.zh: 凡內侍領內東門，次遷勾當禦藥院，而惟吉才進官，眾以為薄，惟吉欣然就職。

translations.literal: Whenever inner attendants headed the Inner East Gate they next managed the Imperial Pharmacy; but Wei Ji had only just been promoted in rank, and many thought the posting slight—Wei Ji gladly took the post.
translations.idiomatic: Inner attendants who headed the Inner East Gate usually moved on to the Imperial Pharmacy; Wei Ji had only just advanced in rank and many thought the assignment beneath him, but he accepted it willingly.

sentences.zh: 再期，以羨餘遷承製。

translations.literal: After two terms, with surplus revenue he was promoted to Palace Manufacturer.
translations.idiomatic: After two terms' surplus receipts he was promoted to palace manufacturer.

sentences.zh: 為趙元昊官告使，還，言元昊驕僭，勢必 叛，請預飭邊備。

translations.literal: Envoy bearing patent for Zhao Yuanhao; on return he said Yuanhao was arrogant and overreaching, would surely rebel, and asked to prepare the border defenses in advance.
translations.idiomatic: As patent envoy to Zhao Yuanhao he returned warning that Yuanhao's arrogance presaged rebellion and urging early border preparations.

sentences.zh: 及元昊寇延州，遣按視鄜延、環慶兩路器甲，並訪攻守利害。

translations.literal: When Yuanhao raided Yan prefecture, sent to inspect armor in Fuyan and Huanqing circuits and also to inquire into attack-and-defend advantages and harms.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanhao attacked Yanzhou he was sent to inspect armor on the Fuyan and Huanqing circuits and to survey their strengths and weaknesses in attack and defense.

sentences.zh: 敵既退，夏竦、韓琦謀自鄜延深入，乘虛擊之，命惟吉募並、汾驍勇，副以土兵，輕 齎赴河外。

translations.literal: After the enemy withdrew, Xia Song and Han Qi planned to advance deep from Fuyan while the enemy was weak and strike; ordered Wei Ji to recruit fierce men from Bing and Fen, with local troops lightly laden to hurry beyond the river.
translations.idiomatic: After the raid ended, Xia Song and Han Qi wished to drive deep from Fuyan and hit Xi Xia while it was exposed; Wei Ji was ordered to recruit crack troops from Bing and Fen, augment them with local militia, and cross the river lightly equipped.

sentences.zh: 惟吉以為我師當持重伺變，不宜馳赴不測以自困，已而元昊果引去。

translations.literal: Wei Ji held that our army should hold steady and watch for changes, and should not rush into the unknown to trap itself; before long Yuanhao indeed withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Ji argued the army should wait on events and keep its weight, not race into uncertainty; Yuanhao soon did withdraw.

sentences.zh: 還奏稱旨，領皇城司，遷內侍省押班、群牧都監，簡陝西冗兵，領軍頭引見司，遷供 備庫使，盡汰軍頭司軍校之罷癃者。

translations.literal: On return his memorial met approval; he took Imperial City Office, promoted to Inner Attendant Service escort leader and herd commissioner, trimmed redundant troops in Shaanxi, took Army-Head Presentation Office, promoted to provision commissioner, and eliminated disabled Army-Head Office instructors.
translations.idiomatic: His report pleased the throne; he took the Imperial City Office, became Inner Service escort leader and herd commissioner, culled Shaanxi's redundant troops, headed the Army-Head Presentation Office, became provision-store commissioner, and cashiered unfit instructors there.

sentences.zh: 同提舉在京諸司庫務，領恩州刺史，為入內都知。

translations.literal: Joint superintendent of capital bureau storehouses, acting Enzhou prefect, and Inner Service director.
translations.idiomatic: He jointly superintended capital storehouses, held Enzhou in name, and became Inner Service director.

sentences.zh: 商胡決，為澶州修河都鈐轄。

translations.literal: When the Shanghu River broke through, made Hedong River repair military commander at Cao prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the Shanghu breach opened, he was made military commander for Cao prefecture river repairs.

sentences.zh: 轉運使施昌言請亟塞，崔嶧以為歲災民困，役宜緩。

translations.literal: Transport commissioner Shi Changyan asked to block it urgently; Cui Yan held that with annual disasters the people were weary and labor should be slow.
translations.idiomatic: Transport commissioner Shi Changyan urged immediate closure; Cui Yan argued that after successive disasters the people were exhausted and work should wait.

sentences.zh: 命惟吉按視，言河可塞而民誠困，財用不足，宜少待之。

translations.literal: Wei Ji was ordered to inspect and said the river could be blocked but the people were truly distressed and funds insufficient; it should wait a little.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to inspect, Wei Ji reported the breach could be sealed but the people were genuinely overburdened and funds short—the work should be deferred.

sentences.zh: 從其議。

translations.literal: They followed his proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The court accepted his view.

sentences.zh: 遷如京使、果州團練使，復領皇城司，卒。

translations.literal: Promoted to Rujing Commissioner and Guozhou regiment commander, again took Imperial City Office, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Rujing commissioner and nominal Guozhou regiment commander, again headed the Imperial City Office, and died.

sentences.zh: 惟吉任事久。

translations.literal: Wei Ji long held office.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Ji had served for many years.

sentences.zh: 頗見親信，而言弗阿徇。

translations.literal: He was much trusted, yet his words did not flatter or follow others.
translations.idiomatic: The throne leaned on him, yet he would not speak to please.

sentences.zh: 張貴妃薨，將治喪皇儀殿，諸宦官皆以為可，獨惟吉曰：“此事幹典禮，須翌日問宰相。”

translations.literal: When Noble Consort Zhang died, they were about to conduct mourning in the Hall of Imperial Rites; all eunuchs said it was permissible—only Wei Ji said, "This matter touches court ritual and must be asked of the chief ministers tomorrow."
translations.idiomatic: At Noble Consort Zhang's death the palace prepared mourning in the Hall of Imperial Rites; every eunuch assented—only Wei Ji said, "This touches state ritual; the chief ministers must be consulted tomorrow."

sentences.zh: 既而宰相不能執議，惟吉深以為非。

translations.literal: Next day the chief ministers could not hold to principle, and Wei Ji deeply thought it wrong.
translations.idiomatic: When the ministers failed to object, Wei Ji considered the decision a grave error.

sentences.zh: 贈昭信軍節度觀察留後。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Military Commissioner and Military Governor of Zhaoxin Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the titles of military commissioner and military governor of Zhaoxin Army.

sentences.zh: 逾月，又贈保順軍節度使，諡忠安。

translations.literal: After more than a month, again posthumously granted Military Commissioner of Baoshun Army, posthumous title Zhong'an.
translations.idiomatic: A month later he was posthumously made military commissioner of Baoshun Army and given the posthumous title Zhong'an, Loyal and Peaceful.

sentences.zh: 養子若水，字益之，以惟吉奏補小黃門，給事章惠太后殿，轉入內高品。

translations.literal: Adopted son Ruoshui, courtesy name Yizhi, through Wei Ji's memorial appointed Junior Yellow Gate attendant, served Empress Dowager Zhanghui's hall, transferred to Inner Service high rank.
translations.idiomatic: His adopted son Ruoshui, courtesy name Yizhi, entered service as a junior Yellow Gate attendant on Wei Ji's recommendation, served in Empress Dowager Zhanghui's hall, and rose to a senior Inner Service rank.

sentences.zh: 王師平貝州，征儂賊，皆以幹敏選為走馬承受。

translations.literal: When imperial armies pacified Beizhou and campaigned against the Nong rebels, in both cases he was chosen for capability and selected as courier commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When the court pacified Beizhou and campaigned against the Nong rebels, his competence won him appointment as courier commissioner on both occasions.

sentences.zh: 賊平，以勞進官，三遷環慶路鈐轄。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified, promoted for merit; after three promotions became Huanqing Circuit military controller.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion ended he was promoted for his service and, through three successive steps, became military controller of Huanqing Circuit.

sentences.zh: 討環州解乜臼族復有功，曆帶禦器械、內侍押班、副都知。

translations.literal: In campaigning against the Jiemiujiu tribe at Huanzhou he again had merit; successively held armed attendant, Inner Attendant Service escort leader, and deputy director.
translations.idiomatic: He won further distinction suppressing the Jiemiujiu tribe at Huanzhou and in time held the posts of armed attendant, Inner Service escort leader, and deputy director.

sentences.zh: 熙寧初，造神臂弓成，神宗禦延和殿臨閱，置鐵甲七十步，俾衛士射，未有中者。

translations.literal: At the start of the Xining era, when the Divine Arm bow was completed, Emperor Shenzong reviewed it in person at the Yanhe Hall, set iron armor at seventy paces, had guards shoot, and none hit.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xining era, when the new Divine Arm bow was ready, Emperor Shenzong inspected it at the Yanhe Hall, set a suit of iron armor seventy paces away, and had the guards shoot—not one hit.

sentences.zh: 若水自請射，連中徹劄。

translations.literal: Ruoshui volunteered to shoot and in succession hit, piercing through the armor plate.
translations.idiomatic: Ruoshui offered to shoot and struck repeatedly, each arrow piercing clean through the plate.

sentences.zh: 建慶壽、寶慈兩宮，典領工作，再遷嘉州防禦使。

translations.literal: Built the Qing Shou and Bao Ci palaces, directed the work, and was again promoted to Jiazhou defense commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He oversaw construction of the Qing Shou and Bao Ci palaces and was promoted again to defense commissioner of Jiazhou.

sentences.zh: 以病蘄解職，領輝州觀察使，提舉四園苑諸司庫務。

translations.literal: On illness requested release from office, held Huizhou observation commissioner, and superintended the four garden parks and various bureau storehouses.
translations.idiomatic: Illness led him to resign his post; he held Huizhou in name and superintended the four imperial garden parks and their storehouses.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈天平軍留後。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously granted Acting Military Commissioner of Tianping Army.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made acting military commissioner of Tianping Army.

sentences.zh: 甘昭吉，字祐之，開封人。

translations.literal: Gan Zhaoji, courtesy name Youzhi, was a man of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Gan Zhaoji, courtesy name Youzhi, came from Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 初以內侍殿頭為英、韶州巡檢，捕盜有功，再遷內殿崇班、京東路都巡檢。

translations.literal: At first as Inner Attendant Service head usher served as Ying and Shao prefectures inspector; capturing bandits had merit; again promoted to Inner Hall Honored Rank and JD Circuit chief inspector.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as head usher in the Inner Attendant Service and as inspector of Ying and Shao prefectures, winning credit for capturing bandits; he was then promoted to Inner Hall Honored Rank and chief inspector of JD Circuit.

sentences.zh: 齊州武衛小校馮坦率營卒二百突入州廳事，欲為變，昭吉單 騎馳往，戒所從將士操兵在外，先獨見亂卒，諭以福禍，令推首惡自贖，眾疑沮不敢動。

translations.literal: Qi prefecture Military Guard company commander Feng Tan led two hundred camp soldiers in a rush into the prefectural hall intending mutiny; Zhaoji alone on horseback galloped there, warned the troops he brought to hold weapons outside, first went alone to see the mutineers, instructed them on fortune and disaster, ordered them to hand over ringleaders to redeem themselves—the crowd hesitated and dared not move.
translations.idiomatic: At Qi prefecture, Military Guard company commander Feng Tan led two hundred camp soldiers in a sudden rush into the prefectural hall to raise a mutiny. Zhaoji rode alone to the scene, ordered the soldiers he had brought to wait armed outside, and went in by himself. He explained the consequences to the rebels and told them to surrender the ringleaders to save themselves; the men wavered and did not dare act.

sentences.zh: 已而操兵者皆入，即共執十餘人，告曰：“此誘我者也。”

translations.literal: Before long the armed men all entered, then together seized more than ten men and reported, saying, "These are the ones who incited us."
translations.idiomatic: Soon his armed men entered as well; the mutineers together seized more than ten men and said, "These are the ones who led us astray."

sentences.zh: 昭吉立殺之，縱 其餘去，州以無事。

translations.literal: Zhaoji immediately executed them, released the rest to go, and the prefecture was unharmed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoji had them executed on the spot, released the rest, and the prefecture passed without further incident.

sentences.zh: 特廷供備庫副使、帶禦器械。

translations.literal: Specially granted assistant provision-store commissioner and armed attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was specially granted the posts of assistant provision-store commissioner and armed attendant at the emperor's side.

sentences.zh: 後內侍省押班闕，仁宗記前功，特以授之。

translations.literal: Later when the Inner Attendant Service escort leader post was vacant, Emperor Renzong remembered his earlier merit and specially granted it to him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Inner Service escort leader's post later fell vacant, Emperor Renzong recalled his earlier service and specially appointed him to it.

sentences.zh: 遷入內副都知。

translations.literal: Promoted to Inner Service deputy director.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to deputy director of the Inner Service.

sentences.zh: 盧守勤，字君錫，開封祥符人。

translations.literal: Lu Shouqin, courtesy name Junxi, was a man of Xiangfu in Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shouqin, courtesy name Junxi, came from Xiangfu in Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 自入內內品累遷禮賓 使、邠寧環慶路鈐轄，還為入內內侍省押班、領昌州刺史。

translations.literal: From Inner Service inner rank successively promoted to protocol commissioner and Binning-Huanqing Circuit military controller; returned to become Inner Attendant Service escort leader and acting Changzhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: From an Inner Service inner rank he rose to protocol commissioner and military controller of Binning-Huanqing Circuit, then returned to the capital as Inner Service escort leader with Changzhou in name.

sentences.zh: 明道中，改葬章懿太后，而舊藏有水，以守勤嚐典葬事，罷為永興軍兵馬鈐轄，徙鄜延路。

translations.literal: In the Mingdao era, when Empress Dowager Zhangyi was reburied, water entered the old tomb; because Shouqin had once managed the burial, he was removed as Yongxing Army military controller and transferred to Fuyan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: During the Mingdao era, water seeped into the old tomb when Empress Dowager Zhangyi was reinterred; because Shouqin had overseen her earlier burial, he was demoted to military controller of Yongxing Army and transferred to Fuyan Circuit.

sentences.zh: 再遷六宅使， 加貴州團練使，進榮州防禦使兼邠寧環慶路安撫都監。

translations.literal: Again promoted to Six Residences commissioner, added Guizhou regiment commander, advanced to Rongzhou defense commissioner and also Binning-Huanqing Circuit pacification superintendent.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to Six Residences commissioner, given Guizhou regiment commander in addition, and advanced to defense commissioner of Rongzhou while also serving as pacification superintendent of Binning-Huanqing Circuit.

sentences.zh: 元昊寇保安軍，守勤率兵擊走之，特遷左騏驥使，移陝西鈐轄。

translations.literal: Yuanhao raided Bao'an Army; Shouqin led troops and drove him off; specially promoted to Left Qiji commissioner and transferred to Shaanxi military controller.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanhao attacked Bao'an Army, Shouqin led troops and repulsed him; he was specially promoted to Left Qiji commissioner and made military controller of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 初，劉平、石元孫被執，守勤撫 膺涕泣不敢出，又嚐易蕃官馬。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Liu Ping and Shi Yuansun were captured, Shouqin beat his breast and wept and dared not go out; he had also once swapped border officer horses.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Liu Ping and Shi Yuansun were taken prisoner, Shouqin beat his breast and wept and would not leave the city; he had also once exchanged horses with a border officer.

sentences.zh: 延州通判計用章勸範雍棄城，將保鄜州，雍欲遣安撫都監李康伯往說賊，不肯行，賊去而守勤、用章更相論奏。

translations.literal: Yanzhou vice prefect Ji Yongzhang urged Fan Yong to abandon the city and fall back to defend Fuzhou; Yong wished to send pacification superintendent Li Kangbo to persuade the enemy, but he refused to go; after the enemy left, Shouqin and Yongzhang repeatedly memorialized against each other.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhou vice prefect Ji Yongzhang urged Fan Yong to abandon the city and withdraw to Fuzhou. Yong wanted to send pacification superintendent Li Kangbo to parley with the enemy, but Kangbo refused. After the raid ended, Shouqin and Yongzhang filed competing accusations against each other.

sentences.zh: 知制誥葉清臣以守勤 擁兵觀望，請正其罪，並按二人。

translations.literal: Drafting edict drafter Ye Qingchen, on grounds that Shouqin held troops and watched without acting, asked that his crime be corrected and that both men be investigated.
translations.idiomatic: Drafting edict drafter Ye Qingchen charged that Shouqin had held his troops back and waited on events, and asked that he be punished and both men investigated.

sentences.zh: 守勤奪防禦使，為湖北都監；

translations.literal: Shouqin was stripped of defense commissioner and made Hubei superintendent;
translations.idiomatic: Shouqin was stripped of his defense commissionership and made superintendent of Hubei;

sentences.zh: 用章除籍，配雷州本城；

translations.literal: Yongzhang was struck from the rolls and exiled to Leizhou proper;
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhang was struck from the rolls and exiled to Leizhou;

sentences.zh: 康伯，均州都監。

translations.literal: Kangbo was made Junzhou superintendent.
translations.idiomatic: Kangbo was made superintendent of Junzhou.

sentences.zh: 久之，復恩州防禦使，遷利州觀察使，曆真定府、定州、北京路鈐轄。

translations.literal: After a long time restored to Enzhou defense commissioner, promoted to Lizhou observation commissioner, and successively held Zhending prefecture, Dingzhou, and Beijing Circuit military controller.
translations.idiomatic: After some years he was restored to defense commissioner of Enzhou, promoted to observation commissioner of Lizhou, and served in turn as military controller of Zhending, Dingzhou, and Beijing Circuit.

sentences.zh: 以左衛大將軍致事，卒，贈保順軍節度使，諡安恪。

translations.literal: Retired as Left Guard grand general, died; posthumously granted Military Commissioner of Baoshun Army, posthumous title Anke.
translations.idiomatic: He retired as Left Guard grand general and died; he was posthumously made military commissioner of Baoshun Army and given the posthumous title Anke, Secure and Respectful.

sentences.zh: 養子昭序。

translations.literal: Adopted son Zhaoxu.
translations.idiomatic: He had an adopted son, Zhaoxu.

sentences.zh: 王守規，真定欒城人，入內都都知守忠之弟。

translations.literal: Wang Shougui was a man of Luancheng in Zhending, younger brother of Inner Service chief director Shouzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shougui came from Luancheng in Zhending and was the younger brother of Inner Service chief director Shouzhong.

sentences.zh: 守忠事真宗，謹願慎密，眷遇最厚。

translations.literal: Shouzhong served Emperor Zhenzong, was cautious, careful, and discreet, and received the deepest favor.
translations.idiomatic: Shouzhong served Emperor Zhenzong with scrupulous discretion and enjoyed the deepest imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 明道時，守規為小黃門，禁中夜半火，守規先覺，自寢殿至後苑皆擊去其鎖，乃 奉仁宗及皇太后至延福宮，回視所經處已成煨燼。

translations.literal: In the Mingdao era, Shougui was a junior Yellow Gate attendant; at midnight fire broke out in the palace; Shougui noticed first, from the sleeping hall to the rear garden knocked off all locks, then escorted Emperor Renzong and the empress dowager to Yanfu Palace; looking back, everywhere he had passed was already ash.
translations.idiomatic: During the Mingdao era, while Shougui was a junior Yellow Gate attendant, a fire broke out in the palace at midnight. He was the first to notice. From the sleeping hall to the rear garden he broke every lock in his path, then escorted Emperor Renzong and the empress dowager to Yanfu Palace; when he looked back, every place he had passed through was already in ashes.

sentences.zh: 翌日，執政候起居，帝曰：“非王守規導朕至此，幾不與卿等相見。”

translations.literal: The next day, when the chief ministers waited on his health, the emperor said, "Had Wang Shougui not guided me here, I would almost not have met with you all."
translations.idiomatic: The next day, when the chief ministers attended him, the emperor said, "If Wang Shougui had not led me out, I might never have seen you again."

sentences.zh: 以功遷入內殿頭。

translations.literal: For the merit he was promoted to Inner Service head usher.
translations.idiomatic: For this service he was promoted to Inner Service head usher.

sentences.zh: 選治京城水，決汴河於公 賈村，決蔡河於四里橋，水患以息。

translations.literal: Chosen to manage capital waters, opened the Bian River at Gongjia Village and the Cai River at Sili Bridge, and water disasters ceased.
translations.idiomatic: He was chosen to manage the capital's waterways, opened the Bian River at Gongjia Village and the Cai River at Sili Bridge, and the flooding subsided.

sentences.zh: 加帶禦器械。

translations.literal: Added armed attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made armed attendant at the emperor's side.

sentences.zh: 積官至宣慶使、康州防禦使、內侍右班副都知。

translations.literal: Through accumulated offices reached Zhaoxing commissioner, Kangzhou defense commissioner, and Inner Attendant Right Bureau deputy director.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to Zhaoxing commissioner, defense commissioner of Kangzhou, and deputy director of the Inner Attendant Right Bureau.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十七，贈昭武軍留後。

translations.literal: He died at age sixty-seven; posthumously granted Acting Military Commissioner of Zhaowu Army.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-seven and was posthumously made acting military commissioner of Zhaowu Army.

sentences.zh: 李憲，字子範，開封 祥符人。

translations.literal: Li Xian, courtesy name Zifan, was a man of Xiangfu in Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xian, courtesy name Zifan, came from Xiangfu in Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 皇祐中，補入內黃門，稍遷供奉官。

translations.literal: In the Huangyou era appointed Inner Yellow Gate attendant, and gradually promoted to tribute commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: During the Huangyou era he entered service as an Inner Yellow Gate attendant and gradually rose to tribute commissioner.

sentences.zh: 神宗即位，曆永興、太原府路走馬承受，數論邊事合旨，幹當後苑。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shenzong took the throne, successively served as Yongxing and Taiyuan prefecture circuit courier commissioner; several times discussed border affairs to the emperor's liking, and managed the rear garden.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shenzong came to the throne, he served in turn as courier commissioner on the Yongxing and Taiyuan circuits; his repeated memorials on frontier affairs pleased the emperor, and he was put in charge of the rear garden.

sentences.zh: 王韶上書請復河湟，命憲往視師，與韶進收河州， 加東染院使，幹當禦藥院。

translations.literal: Wang Shao memorialized asking to recover Hehuang; Xian was ordered to inspect the army; with Shao he advanced and recovered Hezhou; added Eastern Dyeing Bureau commissioner and managed the Imperial Pharmacy.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Shao memorialized to recover the Hehuang region, Xian was sent to inspect the army; he joined Shao in advancing and taking Hezhou, was made Eastern Dyeing Bureau commissioner, and put in charge of the Imperial Pharmacy.

sentences.zh: 復戰牛精穀，拔珂諾城，為熙河經略安撫司幹當公事。

translations.literal: Again fought at Niujing Valley, captured Kenuo Fort, and became senior administrator of the Xihe Pacification and Settlement Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He fought again at Niujing Valley, took Kenuo Fort, and became senior administrator of the Xihe Pacification and Settlement Commission.

sentences.zh: 按視鄜延軍製，行至蒲中，會木征合董氈、鬼章之兵攻破踏白城，殺景思立，圍河 州，詔趣赴之，憲馳至軍。

translations.literal: Inspecting Fuyan army regulations, when he reached Puzhong, Mu Zheng combined Dong Zhan's and Gui Zhang's forces, broke Tabai Fort, killed Jing Sili, and besieged Hezhou; an edict urgently ordered him there, and Xian galloped to the army.
translations.idiomatic: While inspecting Fuyan army regulations he reached Puzhong, where Mu Zheng had joined forces with Dong Zhan and Gui Zhang, stormed Tabai Fort, killed Jing Sili, and besieged Hezhou. Ordered to hurry to the front, Xian galloped to the army.

sentences.zh: 先是，朝廷出黃旗書敕諭將士，如用命破賊者倍賞。

translations.literal: Earlier, the court had issued yellow-flag written edicts instructing the officers and soldiers that those who obeyed orders and defeated the enemy would receive double rewards.
translations.idiomatic: The court had already issued edicts on yellow flags promising double rewards to any soldier who fought with full devotion and broke the enemy.

sentences.zh: 於是憲晨起帳中，張以示眾曰：“此旗，天子所賜也，視此以戰，帝實臨之。”

translations.literal: Thereupon Xian rose early in his tent, unfurled it and showed the crowd, saying, "This flag was bestowed by the Son of Heaven; fight by its sight—the emperor is truly present."
translations.idiomatic: Xian then rose early in his tent, unfurled the flag, and showed it to the troops, saying, "This banner was given by the Son of Heaven. Fight under its sign—the emperor himself watches over you."

sentences.zh: 士爭 呼用命以進。

translations.literal: The soldiers competed in shouting to obey and advance.
translations.idiomatic: The men shouted that they would give their all and pressed forward.

sentences.zh: 督諸將傍山焚族帳，即日通路至河州。

translations.literal: He urged the generals to burn tribal tents along the mountainside, and that same day opened the road to Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: He drove the generals to burn tribal encampments along the mountain slopes and opened a route to Hezhou the same day.

sentences.zh: 賊餘眾保踏白，官軍出與戰，大破之。

translations.literal: The enemy remnant force held Tabai; the government army went out and fought, routing them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining enemy held Tabai; the imperial army sallied forth, fought them, and won a great victory.

sentences.zh: 進至餘川，又破賊堡十餘，木征率酋長八十餘人詣軍門降。

translations.literal: Advancing to Yuchuan, again broke more than ten enemy forts; Mu Zheng led more than eighty chieftains to the army gate to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing to Yuchuan, they stormed more than ten enemy forts; Mu Zheng then came to the camp with more than eighty chieftains and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，以功加 昭宣使、嘉州防禦使。

translations.literal: When victory was reported, for merit added Zhaoxuan commissioner and Jiazhou defense commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When news of the victory arrived, he was promoted for his merit to Zhaoxuan commissioner and defense commissioner of Jiazhou.

sentences.zh: 還，為入內內侍省押班、幹當皇城司。

translations.literal: On return, became Inner Attendant Service escort leader and managed the Imperial City Office.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to the capital he became Inner Service escort leader and head of the Imperial City Office.

sentences.zh: 安南叛，副趙卨招討，未行，卨建言：“朝廷置招討副使，軍事須共議，至節製號令即宜 歸一。”

translations.literal: When Annam rebelled, he served as deputy to Zhao Xu on the pacification campaign; before departing, Xu submitted a proposal: "When the court appoints a deputy pacification commissioner, military affairs must be jointly deliberated, but when it comes to command and orders, authority should be unified."
translations.idiomatic: When Annam rebelled, he served as Zhao Xu's deputy on the pacification campaign. Before they set out, Xu proposed: "A deputy pacification commissioner may deliberate on strategy, but command and orders must rest with one man."

sentences.zh: 憲銜之。

translations.literal: Xian harbored resentment over it.
translations.idiomatic: Xian took this as a personal slight.

sentences.zh: 由是屢紛辨，遂罷憲而令乘驛計議秦鳳、熙河邊事，諸將皆聽節度。

translations.literal: From this they repeatedly disputed; Xian was then removed and ordered to travel by post to deliberate on Qinfeng and Xihe border affairs, and all generals were to obey his command.
translations.idiomatic: Repeated disputes followed, and Xian was removed from the Annam campaign and sent by courier to manage Qinfeng and Xihe frontier affairs, with all generals placed under his command.

sentences.zh: 於是御史中丞鄧潤甫、御史周尹、蔡承禧、彭汝礪極論其不可，又言：“鬼章 之患小，用憲之患大；

translations.literal: Thereupon Censor-in-Chief Deng Runfu and censors Zhou Yin, Cai Chenxi, and Peng Ruli argued most strongly that this was impermissible, also saying, "The trouble from Gui Zhang is small; the trouble from employing Xian is great;"
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Deng Runfu and censors Zhou Yin, Cai Chenxi, and Peng Ruli then protested vehemently, saying, "The threat from Gui Zhang is minor; the threat of putting Xian in command is grave;"

sentences.zh: 憲功不成其禍小，有成功其禍大。”

translations.literal: If Xian's merit does not succeed the harm is small; if he has success the harm is great."
translations.idiomatic: if he fails, the damage will be limited; if he succeeds, the damage will be far greater.

sentences.zh: 章再上，弗聽。

translations.literal: Their memorials were submitted again, but the emperor would not heed them.
translations.idiomatic: They submitted memorial after memorial, but the throne would not listen.

sentences.zh: 冷雞樸誘山後生羌擾邊，木征請自效，眾以為不可。

translations.literal: Leng Jipu incited the post-mountain Sheng Qiang to harass the border; Mu Zheng asked to serve in his own person, and the crowd thought it impermissible.
translations.idiomatic: Leng Jipu incited the Sheng Qiang beyond the mountains to raid the frontier; Mu Zheng offered to serve against them, but most thought it unwise.

sentences.zh: 憲曰：“何傷乎！

translations.literal: Xian said, "What harm is there!"
translations.idiomatic: Xian said, "What is the harm in that?"

sentences.zh: 羌人天性畏服貴 種。”

translations.literal: Qiang people by nature fear and submit to noble stock."
translations.idiomatic: The Qiang by nature fear and defer to men of noble rank.

sentences.zh: 聽之往。

translations.literal: He allowed him to go.
translations.idiomatic: He let him go.

sentences.zh: 木征盛裝以出，眾聳視，皆無鬥誌，師乘之，殺獲萬計，斬冷雞樸。

translations.literal: Mu Zheng went out in full regalia; the crowd stared in awe and all lost fighting spirit; the army seized the moment, killing and capturing by the tens of thousands, and beheaded Leng Jipu.
translations.idiomatic: Mu Zheng appeared in full ceremonial dress; the enemy stared in awe and lost all will to fight. The army pressed the advantage, killing and capturing by the tens of thousands and beheading Leng Jipu.

sentences.zh: 董氈懼，即遣使奉贄效順。

translations.literal: Dong Zhan was afraid and immediately sent envoys bearing tribute to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhan, alarmed, at once sent envoys with tribute to declare his submission.

sentences.zh: 加宣州觀察使、宣政使、入內副都知，又遷宣慶使。

translations.literal: Added Xuanzhou observation commissioner, Xuanzheng commissioner, and Inner Service deputy director; again promoted to Zhaoxing commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was made observation commissioner of Xuanzhou and Xuanzheng commissioner, promoted to Inner Service deputy director, and later to Zhaoxing commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時用兵連年，度支調度不繼，詔憲兼經製財用，裁冗費什六，歲運西山巨木給京師營繕。

translations.literal: At the time warfare continued year after year and the revenue bureau's allocations could not keep up; an edict ordered Xian also to manage finances, cut redundant expenses by six-tenths, and each year transport great timber from the western mountains for capital construction.
translations.idiomatic: War had dragged on for years and the treasury could not keep pace; Xian was ordered to take charge of finances as well. He cut redundant spending by six-tenths and each year shipped great timbers from the western mountains to supply capital construction.

sentences.zh: 賜瑞應坊園宅一區。

translations.literal: Granted one estate in Ruiying Ward.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted an estate in Ruiying Ward.

sentences.zh: 元豐中，五路出師討夏國，憲領熙、秦軍至西市新城。

translations.literal: In the Yuanfeng era, five routes sent armies to campaign against Western Xia; Xian led Xi and Qin forces to Xishi New City.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanfeng era, when five columns marched against Western Xia, Xian led the Xi and Qin armies to Xishi New City.

sentences.zh: 復蘭州，城之，請建為帥府。

translations.literal: Recovered Lanzhou, walled it, and requested that it be made a command headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He recovered Lanzhou, fortified it, and asked that it be established as a command headquarters.

sentences.zh: 帝又詔憲領兵直趣興、靈，董氈亦稱欲往，宜乘機協力入掃巢穴，若興、靈道阻，即過河取涼州。

translations.literal: The emperor again ordered Xian to lead troops straight toward Xing and Ling; Dong Zhan also said he wished to go; they should seize the moment and jointly enter to sweep the nest; if the Xing-Ling route was blocked, then cross the river and take Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor further ordered Xian to drive straight for Xing and Ling; Dong Zhan also declared his willingness to join. They were to strike together and overrun the enemy stronghold; if the route to Xing and Ling proved blocked, they were to cross the river and take Liangzhou instead.

sentences.zh: 乃總兵東上，平夏人於高川石峽。

translations.literal: Thereupon he gathered troops and marched east, defeating Xi Xia forces at Gaochuan Shixia.
translations.idiomatic: He then massed his forces and marched east, defeating Western Xia troops at Gaochuan Shixia.

sentences.zh: 進至屈吳山，營打囉城，趨天都，燒南牟府庫，次葫蘆河而還。

translations.literal: Advanced to Qunwu Mountain, encamped at Daluo Fort, pressed toward Tiandu, burned the Nanmou storehouses, then halted at Hulu River and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to Qunwu Mountain, built camp at Daluo Fort, pressed toward Tiandu, burned the Nanmou storehouses, then withdrew after reaching the Hulu River.

sentences.zh: 憲既不能至靈州，董氈亦失期，師無功。

translations.literal: Xian could not reach Lingzhou, Dong Zhan also missed the rendezvous, and the army achieved nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Xian never reached Lingzhou, Dong Zhan missed his rendezvous, and the campaign came to nothing.

sentences.zh: 憲欲以開蘭、會邀功弭責，同知樞密院孫固曰：“兵法，期而後至者斬。

translations.literal: Xian wished to use the recovery of Lan and Hui to claim merit and deflect blame; Vice Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs Sun Gu said, "By the art of war, he who arrives after the appointed time is beheaded."
translations.idiomatic: Xian hoped to offset blame by claiming credit for recovering Lanzhou and Hui Prefecture. Vice Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs Sun Gu said, "By military law, anyone who arrives after the appointed time is executed."

sentences.zh: 況諸路皆至而憲獨不行，不可赦。”

translations.literal: Moreover, all routes arrived while Xian alone did not go—this cannot be pardoned."
translations.idiomatic: All the other columns reached their objectives while Xian alone failed to advance—this cannot be forgiven.

sentences.zh: 帝以憲猶有 功，但令詰擅還之由，憲以饋餉不接為辭，釋弗誅。

translations.literal: The emperor, on grounds that Xian still had merit, only ordered him questioned on the reason for returning without authorization; Xian pleaded insufficient supplies and was released without execution.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor held that Xian still had some merit and merely demanded an explanation for his unauthorized withdrawal. Xian blamed broken supply lines and was spared punishment.

sentences.zh: 復上再舉之策，兼陳進築五利，且從之。

translations.literal: He again submitted a plan for a renewed campaign, also setting forth five advantages of advancing fortifications, and the emperor partially accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a plan for another campaign, together with five arguments for advancing fortifications, and the court partly accepted his proposal.

sentences.zh: 會李舜舉入奏，具陳師老民困狀，乃罷兵。

translations.literal: When Li Shunju entered court to memorialize and fully described the army's exhaustion and the people's distress, warfare was halted.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Shunju came to court and detailed the exhaustion of the army and the suffering of the people, the campaign was called off.

sentences.zh: 趣憲赴闕，道賜銀帛四千。

translations.literal: Xian was urgently ordered to the capital; on the road he was granted four thousand in silver and silk.
translations.idiomatic: Xian was urgently recalled to court and granted four thousand strings' worth of silver and silk on the road.

sentences.zh: 為涇原經略安撫製置使，給衛三百。

translations.literal: Made Jingyuan pacification and settlement commissioner, granted three hundred guards.
translations.idiomatic: He was made pacification and settlement commissioner of Jingyuan and given three hundred guards.

sentences.zh: 進景福殿使、武信軍留後，使復還熙河，仍兼秦鳳軍馬。

translations.literal: Promoted to Jingfu Hall commissioner and Acting Military Commissioner of Wuxin Army; sent back to Xihe and still concurrently Qinfeng army and horses.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Jingfu Hall commissioner and acting military commissioner of Wuxin Army, sent back to Xihe, and retained command of Qinfeng forces.

sentences.zh: 夏人入蘭州，破西關，降宣慶使。

translations.literal: When Xi Xia forces entered Lanzhou and broke Xiguan, he was demoted to Zhaoxing commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Western Xia raiders entered Lanzhou and broke through Xiguan, he was demoted to Zhaoxing commissioner.

sentences.zh: 憲以蘭州乃西人必爭地，眾數至河外而相羊不進，意必大舉，乃增城守塹壁，樓櫓具備。

translations.literal: Xian held that Lanzhou was ground the western peoples must contest; when the enemy repeatedly reached beyond the river yet lingered without advancing, he judged a major assault certain, and so strengthened the city defenses, moats, walls, towers, and parapets.
translations.idiomatic: Xian judged that Lanzhou was ground Western Xia would fight for. When enemy forces repeatedly massed beyond the river yet hesitated to advance, he expected a major assault and strengthened the city's walls, moats, towers, and parapets.

sentences.zh: 明年冬，夏人果大入，圍蘭州，步騎號八十萬眾，十日不克，糧盡引去。

translations.literal: The next winter, Xi Xia forces indeed invaded on a large scale, besieged Lanzhou, infantry and cavalry claiming eight hundred thousand, and after ten days could not take it; supplies exhausted, they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The next winter Western Xia launched a major invasion and besieged Lanzhou with a force they claimed numbered eight hundred thousand infantry and cavalry. After ten days they could not take the city; their supplies ran out and they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 又詔憲遣間諭阿裏骨結等，且選騎渡河，與賊遇，破之。

translations.literal: Again an edict ordered Xian to send envoys to persuade Ali Gujie and others, and also to select cavalry to cross the river; encountering the enemy, they defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: The court again ordered Xian to send envoys to win over Ali Gujie and others, and to send select cavalry across the river; they met the enemy and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 坐妄奏功狀，罷內省職事。

translations.literal: On account of falsely reporting achievements, he was removed from Inner Service duties.
translations.idiomatic: For falsely reporting his achievements, he was stripped of his Inner Service posts.

sentences.zh: 憲以中人為將，雖能拓地降敵，而罔上害民，終貽患中國雲。

translations.literal: Xian as a eunuch general, though able to expand territory and subdue enemies, deceived superiors and harmed the people, ultimately leaving trouble for China indeed.
translations.idiomatic: The historian's judgment on Xian: as a eunuch general he could expand territory and subdue enemies, yet he deceived his superiors, harmed the people, and in the end brought lasting trouble upon the realm.

sentences.zh: 張茂則，字平甫，開封人。

translations.literal: Zhang Maozi, courtesy name Pingfu, was a man of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Maozi, courtesy name Pingfu, came from Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 初補小黃門，五遷至西頭供奉官，幹當內東門。

translations.literal: At first appointed junior Yellow Gate attendant, after five promotions reached western head tribute commissioner and managed the inner east gate.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as a junior Yellow Gate attendant and, through five promotions, became western head tribute commissioner in charge of the inner east gate.

sentences.zh: 禁庭夜有盜，茂則首登屋以入，既獲賊，遷領禦藥院。

translations.literal: At night there were thieves in the forbidden court; Maozi was first to climb onto the roof to enter; once the thieves were captured, he was promoted to head the Imperial Pharmacy.
translations.idiomatic: When thieves broke into the palace at night, Maozi was the first to climb onto the roof in pursuit; after the culprits were captured, he was put in charge of the Imperial Pharmacy.

sentences.zh: 仁宗不豫，中夜促召，茂則趨入扶衛，左右或欲掩宮門，茂則曰：“事無可慮，何至使中外生疑耶？”

translations.literal: When Emperor Renzong was unwell, at midnight he was urgently summoned; Maozi hurried in to support and guard him; attendants on either side wished to seal the palace gates; Maozi said, "The matter is nothing to worry over—why go so far as to make court and realm suspicious?"
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Renzong fell ill, Maozi was summoned at midnight and rushed in to support and guard him. Some attendants wanted to seal the palace gates, but Maozi said, "There is nothing to fear—why give rise to suspicion inside and outside the palace?"

sentences.zh: 帝疾間，欲處以押班，懇求補外，轉宮苑使、果州團練使， 為永興路兵馬鈐轄。

translations.literal: When the emperor's illness eased, they wished to appoint him escort leader; he earnestly requested an outside post; transferred to palace gardens commissioner and Guozhou regiment commander, and made Yongxing Circuit military controller.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor recovered, the court wished to make him escort leader, but he earnestly asked for a provincial post. He became palace gardens commissioner and nominal Guozhou regiment commander, and was made military controller of Yongxing Circuit.

sentences.zh: 入為內侍押班，再遷副都知。

translations.literal: Entered court as Inner Attendant Service escort leader, again promoted to deputy director.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to the capital as Inner Service escort leader and was promoted again to deputy director.

sentences.zh: 熙寧初，同司馬光相視恩、冀、深、瀛四州生堤及六塔、二股河利害，進入內都知。

translations.literal: At the start of the Xining era, together with Sima Guang inspected the earthen dikes of En, Ji, Shen, and Ying four prefectures and the advantages and harms of Six Pagoda and Ergu River, and was promoted to Inner Service director.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xining era he joined Sima Guang in inspecting the earthen dikes of En, Ji, Shen, and Ying prefectures and the merits and risks of the Six Pagoda and Ergu River projects, and was promoted to Inner Service director.

sentences.zh: 上元夜，宮中火，督眾即撲滅。

translations.literal: On Lantern Festival night, fire broke out in the palace; he urged the crowd and immediately extinguished it.
translations.idiomatic: On Lantern Festival night, when fire broke out in the palace, he rallied the men and had it put out at once.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：“宮禁不驚，帑藏如故，惟忠與力，予固嘉之。”

translations.literal: An edict said, "The palace precincts were undisturbed, the treasury stores remain as before—sole loyalty and exertion; I indeed commend this."
translations.idiomatic: An edict said, "The palace was kept calm and the treasury untouched, thanks to loyal devoted service—I am deeply pleased."

sentences.zh: 賜以窄衣金帶。

translations.literal: He was granted narrow-cut court robes and a gold belt.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted narrow-cut court robes and a gold belt.

sentences.zh: 累乞退休，言受國厚恩，廩食過量，積而未請者七年，乞令三司毀券。

translations.literal: Repeatedly he petitioned to retire, saying he had received the state's deep grace, his grain rations exceeded what he needed, and for seven years surplus had accumulated without claim; he asked that the Three Departments destroy the vouchers.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly asked to retire, explaining that the state had shown him great favor, that he had drawn more grain than he needed, and that surplus rations had piled up unclaimed for seven years; he requested the Three Departments to cancel the vouchers.

sentences.zh: 詔褒之，仍進其官。

translations.literal: An edict commended him and still promoted his rank.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended him in an edict and promoted his rank anyway.

sentences.zh: 哲宗即位，遷寧國軍留後，加兩省都都知。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhezong took the throne, he was transferred to acting military commissioner of Ningguo Army and made director of both Inner Service departments.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhezong ascended the throne, Maozi became acting military commissioner of Ningguo Army and director of both Inner Service departments.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十九。

translations.literal: He died at age seventy-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-nine.

sentences.zh: 茂則性儉素，食不重味，衣裘累十數年不易。

translations.literal: Maozi was frugal and plain by nature; his meals never had more than one flavor, and his fur garments he kept for ten-odd years without changing.
translations.idiomatic: Maozi was frugal and unpretentious: he never served more than one dish at a meal, and he wore the same fur coat for more than ten years.

sentences.zh: 紹聖論元祐人，以茂則嚐預任使，追貶左監門衛將軍，崇寧中入黨籍。

translations.literal: During Shaosheng, when Yuanyou men were condemned, because Maozi had once served in appointments, he was posthumously demoted to Left Guardian of the Gate Command general; in Chongning he entered the faction register.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shaosheng backlash against Yuanyou officials, Maozi was posthumously demoted to Left Guardian of the Gate Command because he had once held office under that faction; in the Chongning era his name was entered on the proscribed list.

sentences.zh: 宋用臣，字正卿，開封人。

translations.literal: Song Yongchen, courtesy name Zhengqing, was a man of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Song Yongchen, courtesy name Zhengqing, came from Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 為人有精思強力，以父蔭隸職內省。

translations.literal: As a man of keen thought and strong capability, through his father's privilege he entered service in the Inner Department.
translations.idiomatic: A man of keen mind and tireless energy, he entered the Inner Department through his father's privilege.

sentences.zh: 神宗建東、西府，築京城，建尚書省，起太學，立原廟，導洛通汴，凡大工役，悉董其事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shenzong built the eastern and western offices, walled the capital, built the Department of State Affairs, established the Imperial University, erected the Primary Temple, and opened the Luo River to connect with the Bian Canal—for all major works he supervised the affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenzong built the eastern and western offices, rebuilt the capital walls, raised the Department of State Affairs, founded the Imperial University, established the Primary Temple, and cut the Luo River channel to join the Bian Canal, Yongchen supervised every major project.

sentences.zh: 性敏 給，善傳詔令，故多訪以外事。

translations.literal: Quick and resourceful in nature, skilled at transmitting edicts, he was therefore often consulted on outside affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Quick-witted and agile, he excelled at delivering imperial edicts and was often consulted on matters beyond the palace.

sentences.zh: 同列悉籍以進，朝士之乏廉節者，往往諂附之，權勢震赫一時。

translations.literal: His colleagues all reported through him; court officials lacking integrity often flattered and attached themselves to him, and for a time his power and prestige were overwhelming.
translations.idiomatic: Colleagues routed everything through him; officials who lacked integrity often fawned on him, and for a time his power was unrivaled.

sentences.zh: 積勞至登州防禦使，加宣政使。

translations.literal: Through accumulated service he rose to defender of Deng Prefecture and was made Xuanzheng commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Through long service he reached the rank of defender of Deng Prefecture and was made Xuanzheng commissioner.

sentences.zh: 元祐初，言者論其罪，降為皇城使， 謫監滁州、太平州酒稅。

translations.literal: At the start of Yuanyou, critics indicted his crimes; he was reduced to Imperial City commissioner and demoted to supervise wine tax at Chuzhou and Taiping prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yuanyou era, critics indicted his misconduct; he was reduced to Imperial City commissioner and sent to supervise wine tax at Chuzhou and Taiping.

sentences.zh: 四年，主管靈仙觀。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he was put in charge of the Lingxian Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was assigned to oversee the Lingxian Temple.

sentences.zh: 紹聖初，召為內侍押班，進瀛州刺史。

translations.literal: Early in Shaosheng, he was recalled as Inner Attendant Service escort leader and promoted to prefect of Ying Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shaosheng he was recalled as Inner Attendant Service escort leader and promoted to prefect of Ying Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 王中正，字希烈，開封人。

translations.literal: Wang Zhongzheng, courtesy name Xilie, was a man of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhongzheng, courtesy name Xilie, came from Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 因父任補入內黃門，遷赴延福宮學詩書、曆算。

translations.literal: Through his father's position he was admitted as Inner Yellow Gate attendant and transferred to Yanfu Palace to study classics, histories, and calendrical calculation.
translations.idiomatic: Through his father's office he entered as an Inner Yellow Gate attendant and was sent to Yanfu Palace to study the classics, histories, and calendrical science.

sentences.zh: 仁宗嘉其才，命置左右。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong admired his talent and ordered him placed at his side.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong admired his ability and had him kept at his side.

sentences.zh: 慶曆衛士之變，中正援弓矢即殿西督捕射，賊悉就擒，時年甫十八，人頗壯之。

translations.literal: During the Qingli guard mutiny, Zhongzheng took bow and arrows at once to the west of the hall to supervise the hunt and shooting; the bandits were all seized. He was only eighteen, and people greatly admired him.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qingli guard mutiny, Zhongzheng seized bow and arrows and, from the west side of the hall, directed the pursuit and shooting; the rebels were all captured. He was only eighteen, and men admired his courage.

sentences.zh: 遷東頭供奉官，曆幹當禦藥院、鄜延、環慶路公事，分治河東邊事。

translations.literal: Promoted to eastern head tribute commissioner, he served in turn at the Imperial Pharmacy and on official business for Fuyan and Huanqing circuits, dividing control of Hedong border affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to eastern head tribute commissioner, he served at the Imperial Pharmacy and on official business for Fuyan and Huanqing circuits, sharing responsibility for Hedong border affairs.

sentences.zh: 破西人有功，帶禦器械。

translations.literal: For merit in defeating western barbarians, he was granted Imperial equipage.
translations.idiomatic: For defeating the western tribes he was granted Imperial equipage.

sentences.zh: 神宗將復熙河，命之規度。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shenzong was about to recover the Xi He region, he was ordered to survey and plan.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenzong prepared to recover the Xi He region, Zhongzheng was ordered to survey and plan the campaign.

sentences.zh: 還言：“熙河譬乳虎抱玉，乘爪牙未備，可取也。”

translations.literal: On return he said, "The Xi He region is like a suckling tiger holding jade—while its claws and fangs are not yet ready, it can be taken."
translations.idiomatic: On his return he said, "Xi He is like a cub tiger clutching jade—while its claws and fangs are not yet grown, it can be seized."

sentences.zh: 遂從王韶入熙河，治城壁守具，以功遷作坊使、嘉州團練使，擢內侍押班。

translations.literal: He then followed Wang Shao into Xi He, prepared walls and defensive equipment, and for merit was promoted to workshop commissioner and Guozhou regiment commander, and elevated to Inner Attendant Service escort leader.
translations.idiomatic: He then followed Wang Shao into Xi He, built walls and prepared defenses, and for his service was promoted to workshop commissioner and Guozhou regiment commander and made Inner Attendant Service escort leader.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃圍茂州，詔率陝西兵援之，圍解。

translations.literal: When Tibetans besieged Mao Prefecture, an edict ordered him to lead Shaanxi troops to aid them, and the siege was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: When Tibetans besieged Mao Prefecture, he was ordered to lead Shaanxi troops to the relief, and the siege was broken.

sentences.zh: 自石泉至茂州，謂之隴東路，土田肥美，西羌據有之，中正不能討。

translations.literal: From Shiquan to Mao Prefecture was called the Longdong Road; the land was fertile and fine, and the western Qiang held it, but Zhongzheng could not subdue them.
