translations.idiomatic: The route from Shiquan to Mao Prefecture was known as the Longdong Road—fertile country held by the western Qiang—and Zhongzheng could not drive them out.

sentences.zh: 乃因吐蕃入寇，言：“其路經靜州等族，棒僻不通，邇 年商旅稍往來，故外蕃因以乘間。

translations.literal: Then, taking advantage of a Tibetan incursion, he said, "That route passes through the Jingzhou tribes; the path is rough and blocked. In recent years merchants have begun to travel back and forth, so outer barbarians have thus found an opening."
translations.idiomatic: Then, using a Tibetan raid as his pretext, he said, "That route runs through the Jingzhou tribes by rough, impassable paths. In recent years merchants have begun to travel it, giving outer tribes their chance to strike."

sentences.zh: 縣至綿與茂，道裏均，而龍安有都巡檢，緩急可倚仗。

translations.literal: From the county seat to Mian and Mao the distance was equal, and Long'an had a patrol commander who could be relied on in emergencies.
translations.idiomatic: The distance from the county seat to Mian and Mao was the same, and Long'an had a patrol commander who could be counted on in an emergency.

sentences.zh: 請割石泉隸綿，而窒其故道。”

translations.literal: He requested that Shiquan be transferred to Mian and the old route blocked."
translations.idiomatic: He asked that Shiquan be placed under Mian and the old route closed off.

sentences.zh: 從之，隴東遂不可得。

translations.literal: The request was granted, and Longdong was thus unobtainable forever after.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed, and the Longdong route was lost for good.

sentences.zh: 還，使熙河經畫鬼 章，進昭宣使、入內副都知。

translations.literal: On return he was sent to Xi He to plan against Gui Zhang, promoted to Zhaoxuan commissioner and Inner Deputy Director.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was dispatched to Xi He to manage operations against Gui Zhang, and was promoted to Zhaoxuan commissioner and Inner Deputy Director.

sentences.zh: 元豐初，提舉教畿縣保甲將兵捕賊盜巡檢，獻民兵伍保法，請於村疃及縣以時閱習，悉行其言。

translations.literal: Early in Yuanfeng, he was put in charge of drilling the capital counties' baojia militia to capture bandits on patrol, presented the militia five-family system, and requested periodic drills in villages and counties; all his proposals were adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuanfeng he oversaw drilling the capital counties' baojia militia for bandit patrols, submitted the militia five-family system, and asked that villages and counties drill on schedule; the court adopted all of it.

sentences.zh: 復往鄜延、環慶經製邊事，詔凡所須用度，令兩路取給，無限多寡。

translations.literal: Again he went to Fuyan and Huanqing to manage border affairs; an edict ordered that all expenditures needed on the two circuits be drawn without limit on amount.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to Fuyan and Huanqing to manage border affairs, with an edict that both circuits supply whatever he needed, without limit.

sentences.zh: 既行，又稱麵受詔，所過募禁兵，願從者將之，主者不敢違。

translations.literal: After he set out, he also claimed to have received the edict in person; wherever he passed he recruited palace guard troops, and those willing to follow he took along—the officials in charge did not dare refuse.
translations.idiomatic: Once underway he also claimed a face-to-face edict; wherever he went he recruited palace guards and took along any who volunteered, and local officials did not dare refuse.

sentences.zh: 問罪西夏，以中正簽書涇原路經略司事。

translations.literal: To demand punishment of Western Xia, Zhongzheng was made signing secretary of the Jingyuan Circuit frontier commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When the court moved to punish Western Xia, Zhongzheng was made signing secretary of the Jingyuan frontier headquarters.

sentences.zh: 詔五路之師皆會靈州，中正失期，糧道不繼，士卒多死，命權分屯鄜延並邊城砦，以俟後舉。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the armies of five routes to assemble at Ling Prefecture; Zhongzheng missed the deadline, supply lines failed, and many soldiers died. He was ordered provisionally to divide encampments among the border fortresses of Fuyan, awaiting a later campaign.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the five-route armies to assemble at Ling Prefecture. Zhongzheng missed the deadline, supplies failed, and many soldiers died. He was told to hold scattered camps along the Fuyan border and wait for another attempt.

sentences.zh: 自請罷省職，遷金州觀察 使、提舉西太一宮，坐前敗貶秩。

translations.literal: At his own request he was relieved of provincial rank, transferred to military commissioner of Jin Prefecture and put in charge of the Great Western One Palace, demoted in rank on account of the earlier defeat.
translations.idiomatic: At his own request he gave up his provincial post, became military commissioner of Jin Prefecture and overseer of the Great Western One Palace, and was demoted for the earlier defeat.

sentences.zh: 元祐初，言者再論其將王師二十萬，公違詔書之罪，劉摯比中正與李憲、宋用臣、石得一為四凶，又貶秩兩等。

translations.literal: At the start of Yuanyou, critics again indicted him for leading two hundred thousand imperial troops in open violation of the edict; Liu Zhe compared Zhongzheng with Li Xian, Song Yongchen, and Shi Deyi as the Four Evildoers, and his rank was reduced by two more grades.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuanyou, critics again charged him with leading two hundred thousand imperial troops in open defiance of the edict. Liu Zhe grouped Zhongzheng with Li Xian, Song Yongchen, and Shi Deyi as the Four Evildoers, and his rank was cut by two more grades.

sentences.zh: 久之，提舉崇福 宮。

translations.literal: After some time, he was put in charge of Chongfu Palace.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was assigned to oversee Chongfu Palace.

sentences.zh: 紹聖初，復嘉州團練使。

translations.literal: Early in Shaosheng, he was restored to Guozhou regiment commander.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shaosheng he was restored to Guozhou regiment commander.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十一。

translations.literal: He died at age seventy-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-one.

sentences.zh: 李舜舉，字公輔，開封人。

translations.literal: Li Shunju, courtesy name Gongfu, was a man of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shunju, courtesy name Gongfu, came from Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 世為內侍，曾祖神福，事太宗以信謹終始。

translations.literal: For generations the family served as eunuchs; his great-grandfather Shenfu served Emperor Taizong with faithful care from start to finish.
translations.idiomatic: His family had served as eunuchs for generations; his great-grandfather Shenfu attended Emperor Taizong with faithful diligence from first to last.

sentences.zh: 舜舉少補黃門，仁宗使督工冶金為器，既成，有羨數並上之，帝嘉其不欺。

translations.literal: Shunju entered as Yellow Gate attendant while young; the emperor had him oversee smelting metal into vessels. When finished, there was surplus metal which he reported together with the vessels; the emperor praised his honesty.
translations.idiomatic: Shunju entered service young as a Yellow Gate attendant. Emperor Renzong had him supervise the smelting of metal into vessels; when the work was done, he reported the surplus metal along with the vessels, and the emperor praised his honesty.

sentences.zh: 出為秦鳳路走馬承受。

translations.literal: He went out as courier-commissioner of Qinfeng Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as courier-commissioner of Qinfeng Circuit.

sentences.zh: 英宗立，奏事京師。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong took the throne, he reported affairs at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yingzong ascended the throne, Shunju came to the capital to report on affairs.

sentences.zh: 會帝不豫，內謁者止之宮門，舜舉曰：“天子新即位，使者從邊方來，不得一見而去，何以慰遠人！”

translations.literal: When the emperor was unwell, inner ushers stopped him at the palace gate. Shunju said, "The Son of Heaven has just ascended; an envoy comes from the border—if he cannot get one audience before leaving, how can distant men be comforted!"
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor fell ill, inner ushers barred him at the palace gate. Shunju said, "The Son of Heaven has only just taken the throne; an envoy has come from the frontier—if he cannot even receive one audience before leaving, how will distant subjects be reassured!"

sentences.zh: 謁者以聞，亟召對，帝意良悅。

translations.literal: The usher reported it; he was quickly summoned for audience, and the emperor was well pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The usher reported this; Shunju was summoned at once for audience, and the emperor was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 因言：“承受公事，以察守將不法為職，而終更論最，乃使帥臣保任，乞免之。”

translations.literal: He then said, "The courier's duties are to investigate law-breaking by regional commanders, yet at term's end the evaluation of merit makes the circuit commander guarantee the appointee—I beg that this be abolished."
translations.idiomatic: He then said, "A courier-commissioner's duty is to watch for misconduct by regional commanders, yet at the end of a term the circuit commander must vouch for him in the merit review—I ask that this rule be abolished."

sentences.zh: 遂刪舊制。

translations.literal: The old regulation was thereupon deleted.
translations.idiomatic: The old regulation was thereupon struck from the books.

sentences.zh: 熙寧中，曆幹當內東門、禦藥院、講筵閣、實錄院。

translations.literal: During Xining he served in turn at the inner east gate, Imperial Pharmacy, Lecture Pavilion, and Veritable Records Institute.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xining era he served in turn at the inner east gate, the Imperial Pharmacy, the Lecture Pavilion, and the Veritable Records Institute.

sentences.zh: 郭逵討交州，以為廣西幹當公事，軍中之政得與講畫，或疾置入朝，稟受成算。

translations.literal: When Guo Kui campaigned against Jiaozhou, Shunju was made Guangxi affairs manager; he could join in planning military policy, and sometimes urgent-dispatched to court to receive the approved strategy.
translations.idiomatic: When Guo Kui campaigned against Jiaozhou, Shunju was made Guangxi affairs manager; he took part in planning military affairs and sometimes rode posthaste to court to receive the approved strategy.

sentences.zh: 會逵貶，亦降左藏庫副使，以文思院使領文州刺史、帶禦器械。

translations.literal: When Kui was demoted, he too was reduced to deputy commissioner of the Left Treasury and, as Wensi Institute commissioner, held the nominal prefect of Wenz Prefecture and Imperial equipage.
translations.idiomatic: When Kui was demoted, Shunju was reduced to deputy commissioner of the Left Treasury and, as Wensi Institute commissioner, held the nominal title of prefect of Wenz Prefecture with Imperial equipage.

sentences.zh: 進內侍押班，製置涇原軍馬。

translations.literal: Promoted to Inner Attendant Service escort leader, he was made Jingyuan military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Inner Attendant Service escort leader, he was put in charge of Jingyuan forces.

sentences.zh: 五路師出無功，議再舉，李憲督饋糧，言受密詔，自都轉運使以下乏軍興者皆聽斬。

translations.literal: The five-route expedition achieved nothing; there was talk of another campaign. Li Xian supervised supply and claimed a secret edict authorizing him to execute anyone from the transport commissioner downward who failed in military provisions.
translations.idiomatic: The five-route campaign ended without success, yet some urged another try. Li Xian supervised supplies and claimed a secret edict empowering him to execute anyone from the transport commissioner down who fell short in provisioning the army.

sentences.zh: 民懲前日之役多死於凍餒，皆憚行，出錢百緡不能雇一夫，相聚立柵山澤不受 調，吏往逼呼，輒毆擊，解州至械縣令以督之，不能集。

translations.literal: The people, chastened by the multitudes who died of cold and hunger in the previous campaign, all feared to go; one hundred strings of cash could not hire a single laborer. They gathered to erect stockades in mountains and marshes and refused mobilization; officials sent to press and summon were beaten. From Jie Prefecture to Xi Prefecture officials even shackled magistrates to compel them—still they could not assemble the men.
translations.idiomatic: Still smarting from the last campaign, in which multitudes died of cold and hunger, the people dreaded going; a hundred strings of cash could not hire one man. They banded together in mountains and marshes behind stockades and refused conscription; officials sent to press them were beaten. In Jie Prefecture magistrates were even shackled to force compliance—and still the levies could not be filled.

sentences.zh: 舜舉入奏其事，乃罷兵。

translations.literal: Shunju entered and memorialized the matter, and the campaign was halted.
translations.idiomatic: Shunju memorialized the situation at court, and the campaign was called off.

sentences.zh: 退詣中書，王珪迎勞之曰：“朝廷以邊事屬押班及李留後，無西顧之憂矣。”

translations.literal: Retiring, he went to the Secretariat, where Wang Gui welcomed and comforted him, saying, "The court has entrusted border affairs to the Escort Leader and Vice Military Commissioner Li—there is no worry about the west."
translations.idiomatic: On his way out he stopped at the Secretariat, where Wang Gui greeted him warmly and said, "The court has put the western frontier in the hands of the Escort Leader and Vice Military Commissioner Li—we need not worry about the west."

sentences.zh: 舜舉 曰：“四郊多壘，此卿大夫之辱，相公當國，而以邊事屬二內臣，可乎？

translations.literal: Shunju said, "When the four borders bristle with fortresses, it is the shame of the ministers. The grand councilor holds the state—yet you entrust border affairs to two eunuchs—is that acceptable?"
translations.idiomatic: Shunju replied, "When enemies press on every side, it is the shame of the court's ministers. You hold the reins of government—yet you leave the frontier to two eunuchs. Is that fitting?

sentences.zh: 內臣正宜供禁庭灑掃之職，豈可當將帥之任！”

translations.literal: Eunuchs should rightly perform the duties of sweeping and cleaning within the forbidden precincts—how can they bear the responsibilities of generals and commanders!"
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs are meant to sweep and keep the inner palace—how can they stand in for generals and commanders!

sentences.zh: 聞者代珪慚焉。

translations.literal: Those who heard it were ashamed on Gui's behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Those who heard it were ashamed for Wang Gui.

sentences.zh: 轉嘉州團練使。

translations.literal: Transferred to Guozhou regiment commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Guozhou regiment commander.

sentences.zh: 沈括城永樂，遣舜舉計議，被圍急，斷衣襟作奏曰：“臣死無所恨，願朝廷勿輕此賊。”

translations.literal: When Shen Kuo fortified Yongle, he sent Shunju to consult; besieged in desperate straits, he tore off his robe collar to write a memorial: "Your servant dies without regret; I pray the court not underestimate this enemy."
translations.idiomatic: When Shen Kuo fortified Yongle, he sent Shunju to advise; under tight siege, Shunju tore a strip from his robe collar and wrote a memorial: "I die without regret, but I beg the court not to underestimate this enemy."

sentences.zh: 尋以死聞，贈昭信軍節度使，諡曰忠敏。

translations.literal: Shortly word came of his death; he was posthumously granted military commissioner of Zhaoxin Army with posthumous name Zhongmin (Loyal and Keen).
translations.idiomatic: Soon word came that he had died; he was posthumously made military commissioner of Zhaoxin Army with the posthumous name Zhongmin (Loyal and Keen).

sentences.zh: 舜舉資性安重，與人言未嚐及宮省事。

translations.literal: Shunju's nature was steady and sober; in conversation with others he never touched palace affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Shunju was steady and reserved by nature; in conversation he never spoke of palace business.

sentences.zh: 頗覽書傳，能文辭筆劄。

translations.literal: He read widely in books and classics and could write literary prose and letters.
translations.idiomatic: He read widely and could compose polished prose and letters.

sentences.zh: 在禦藥院十四年，神宗嚐書“李舜舉公忠奉上，恭勤檢身，始終惟一，以安以榮。”

translations.literal: During fourteen years at the Imperial Pharmacy, Emperor Shenzong once wrote, "Li Shunju is loyal and devoted in serving above, reverent and diligent in keeping himself, from beginning to end one and the same—from peace to honor."
translations.idiomatic: During his fourteen years at the Imperial Pharmacy, Emperor Shenzong once wrote of him, "Li Shunju serves with public loyalty and private devotion, keeps himself reverent and diligent, and from first to last is unchanged—in peace as in honor."

sentences.zh: 十九字賜之。

translations.literal: These nineteen characters were granted to him.
translations.idiomatic: These nineteen characters were bestowed on him as an imperial gift.

sentences.zh: 石得一，開封人。

translations.literal: Shi Deyi was a man of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Deyi came from Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 為內侍黃門，累官內殿承製。

translations.literal: As Inner Attendant Yellow Gate, he rose through ranks to Inner Hall draftsman.
translations.idiomatic: Entering as an Inner Attendant Yellow Gate, he rose through the ranks to Inner Hall draftsman.

sentences.zh: 神宗時，帶禦器械、管幹龍圖天章寶文閣、皇城司，四遷入內副都知。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Shenzong he held Imperial equipage, managed the Longtu, Tianzhang, and Baowen pavilions and the Imperial City Bureau, and through four promotions became Inner Deputy Director.
translations.idiomatic: Under Shenzong he held Imperial equipage, managed the Longtu, Tianzhang, and Baowen pavilions and the Imperial City Bureau, and after four promotions became Inner Deputy Director.

sentences.zh: 元祐初，領成州團練使，罷內省職。

translations.literal: At the start of Yuanyou he held the nominal Guozhou regiment commander and was relieved of Inner Department duties.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuanyou he held the nominal rank of Guozhou regiment commander and was removed from Inner Department duties.

sentences.zh: 御史劉 摯言：“得一頃筦皇城，恣其殘刻，縱遣邏者，所在棋布，張阱設網，以無為有，以虛為實。

translations.literal: Censor Liu Zhe said, "When Deyi recently managed the Imperial City, he indulged cruelty and harshness, sent out scouts far and wide, and everywhere laid traps and nets, making something out of nothing and the empty into the real."
translations.idiomatic: Censor Liu Zhe said, "While Deyi ran the Imperial City, he indulged cruelty, sent spies everywhere, and spread traps across the land, turning nothing into something and fiction into fact."

sentences.zh: 朝廷大吏及富家小人，飛語朝上，暮入狴犴，上下惴恐，不能自保，至 相顧以目者殆十年。”

translations.literal: High officials of the court and wealthy commoners—anonymous reports reached court in the morning and by evening they were in prison. Above and below trembled in fear and could not protect themselves; people even exchanged glances for nearly ten years."
translations.idiomatic: High officials and wealthy commoners alike faced anonymous accusations in the morning and prison by evening. Court and country lived in fear, unable to protect themselves; for nearly ten years people dared only exchange glances.

sentences.zh: 坐降左藏庫使，卒。

translations.literal: On this account he was demoted to Left Treasury commissioner and died.
translations.idiomatic: For this he was demoted to Left Treasury commissioner and later died.

sentences.zh: 紹聖中，贈隨州觀察使。

translations.literal: During Shaosheng he was posthumously granted military commissioner of Sui Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: During Shaosheng he was posthumously made military commissioner of Sui Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 梁從吉，字君祐，開封人。

translations.literal: Liang Congji, courtesy name Junyou, was a man of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Congji, courtesy name Junyou, came from Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 補入內高班。

translations.literal: Admitted as Inner Senior Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as an Inner Senior Attendant.

sentences.zh: 王則反，奉命宣慰，還言：“小寇無多 慮，諸將之兵足以翦除，若得重臣統其事，不崇朝可平矣。”

translations.literal: When Wang Ze rebelled, Congji was ordered to announce comfort; on return he said, "The small bandits are nothing to worry over—the generals' troops are sufficient to cut them down; if only a high minister were appointed to command the matter, they could be pacified before noon."
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Ze rebelled, Congji was sent to announce imperial reassurance; on his return he said, "These petty rebels are no great concern—the generals' troops are enough to destroy them. Put a senior minister in command and they can be crushed before noon."

sentences.zh: 於是仁宗以文彥博為安撫招討使。

translations.literal: Thereupon Emperor Renzong made Wen Yanbo Grand Pacifier and Campaign Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Emperor Renzong appointed Wen Yanbo Grand Pacifier and Campaign Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 賊平，又奏請分河北為路，每路以一帥府統之，遂建魏、鎮、定、瀛 四帥。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified, he again memorialized to divide Hebei into circuits, each with one commanding prefecture overseeing it, and thus Wei's, Zhen's, Ding's, and Ying's four command seats were established.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels were crushed, he memorialized to divide Hebei into circuits, each under a single command seat; Wei, Zhen, Ding, and Ying were thus established as four frontier commands.

sentences.zh: 熙寧初，為邠寧環慶路駐泊兵馬鈐轄。

translations.literal: Early in Xining he was commander of stationed forces of Binning and Huanqing circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xining era he became commander of stationed forces on the Binning and Huanqing frontier.

sentences.zh: 夏人寇大順城，圍慶州七砦，從吉率兵八百餘人與戰，獲其酋領。

translations.literal: When the Xia attacked Dashuncheng and besieged seven fortresses of Qing Prefecture, Congji led more than eight hundred men to fight and captured their chieftain.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tangut raided Dashuncheng and besieged seven fortresses around Qing Prefecture, Congji led more than eight hundred men into battle and captured an enemy chieftain.

sentences.zh: 又討平寧州叛卒，以功升都鈐轄，累官皇城使。

translations.literal: He also suppressed rebellious soldiers in Ning Prefecture and, for merit, was promoted to chief controller, rising through offices to Imperial City commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He also put down mutinous troops in Ning Prefecture and, for his service, was promoted to chief controller, eventually reaching Imperial City commissioner.

sentences.zh: 從高 遵裕至靈武，督士卒攻城，身被創甚，進入內押班，遷永州團練使，為副都知。

translations.literal: Following Gao Zunyu to Lingwu, he supervised troops in storming the city; his body was severely wounded; promoted to Inner Attendant Service escort leader, transferred to Yongzhou regiment commander, and made deputy director.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Gao Zunyu to Lingwu and directed the assault on the city, suffering severe wounds. He was promoted to Inner Attendant Service escort leader, made Yongzhou regiment commander, and appointed deputy director.

sentences.zh: 元祐中卒，贈成德軍節度使，諡曰敏恪。

translations.literal: He died in Yuanyou and was posthumously granted military commissioner of Chengde Army with posthumous name Minke (Keen and Respectful).
translations.idiomatic: He died during the Yuanyou era and was posthumously made military commissioner of Chengde Army with the posthumous name Minke (Keen and Respectful).

sentences.zh: 劉惟簡，開封人，由入內黃門 積官至昭宣使、康州刺史、高陽關路兵馬都監，為入內押班。

translations.literal: Liu Weijian, a man of Kaifeng, through Inner Yellow Gate service rose through offices to Zhaoxuan commissioner, nominal prefect of Kang Prefecture, military supervisor of Gaoyang Pass Road, and Inner Attendant Service escort leader.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Weijian of Kaifeng entered as an Inner Yellow Gate attendant and rose through the ranks to Zhaoxuan commissioner, nominal prefect of Kang Prefecture, military supervisor of Gaoyang Pass Road, and Inner Attendant Service escort leader.

sentences.zh: 英宗初立，惟簡自河北來朝，請對寢門，內謁者難之，獨引見皇太后。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong had just taken the throne, Weijian came from Hebei to attend court, requested audience at the sleeping gate; inner ushers found it difficult, but he alone was led to see the Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yingzong had just ascended the throne, Weijian came from Hebei to court and asked for audience at the sleeping gate. The inner ushers balked, but he was at last brought before the Empress Dowager alone.

sentences.zh: 惟簡立福寧殿下，雨沾衣不退， 帝起坐幃中，望見呼問曰：“諸路如汝者幾人，何以獨來？”

translations.literal: Weijian stood below the Hall of Eternal Tranquility; rain soaked his clothes but he did not withdraw. The emperor rose from within the canopy, saw him from afar, called and asked, "How many men like you are there on the various routes—why have you come alone?"
translations.idiomatic: Weijian stood below the Hall of Eternal Tranquility as rain soaked his clothes, yet he would not leave. The emperor rose within the curtained bed and, seeing him from afar, called out, "How many men like you are there on the frontier circuits—and why have you come alone?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：“陛下新即位，臣來自邊塞，未瞻天表，不敢輒還，不知其他。”

translations.literal: He answered, "Your Majesty has just ascended the throne; your servant comes from the border, has not yet beheld the imperial countenance, and dares not return on his own—I know nothing of the others."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Your Majesty has only just taken the throne. I come from the frontier and have not yet seen your face; I dared not turn back on my own. As for the others, I do not know."

sentences.zh: 帝歎曰：“小臣知所守如此。”

translations.literal: The emperor sighed and said, "A petty official who knows what to keep to—so."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sighed and said, "Even a minor official can hold to his duty like this."

sentences.zh: 識其姓名屏間。

translations.literal: He had his name noted on a screen.
translations.idiomatic: He had Weijian's name written on a screen to remember him.

sentences.zh: 他日，神宗覽所題屏，擢幹當延福宮，自是蒙親信。

translations.literal: Another day, Emperor Shenzong viewed the inscription on the screen and promoted him to manage Yanfu Palace; from then on he enjoyed the emperor's trust.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Shenzong saw the name on the screen, he promoted Weijian to manage Yanfu Palace, and from then on treated him with personal trust.

sentences.zh: 交人叛，詔馳驛至桂州審視事勢，還言：“帥臣劉彝貪功生事，罪當誅。

translations.literal: When the Annamese rebelled, an edict ordered him to ride posthaste to Guilin to examine the situation; on return he said, "The circuit commander Liu Yi, greedy for merit, stirred up trouble—his crime deserves execution."
translations.idiomatic: When the Annamese rebelled, he was ordered to ride posthaste to Guilin to assess the situation. On his return he reported, "The circuit commander Liu Yi, greedy for glory, provoked the crisis—he deserves death."

sentences.zh: 乾德狂童，頸不足係。”

translations.literal: The reckless youth Qian De—hardly worth putting a halter around his neck.
translations.idiomatic: As for the reckless youth Qian De, his neck is scarcely worth the rope.

sentences.zh: 帝信之。

translations.literal: The emperor believed him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor believed him.

sentences.zh: 郭逵、趙卨南征，以為行營承受。

translations.literal: When Guo Kui and Zhao Jie campaigned south, he was made campaign courier-commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Guo Kui and Zhao Jie marched south, Weijian was made campaign courier-commissioner.

sentences.zh: 逵、卨被謫，惟簡亦奪一官。

translations.literal: When Kui and Jie were demoted, Weijian also lost one rank.
translations.idiomatic: When Kui and Jie were demoted, Weijian lost one rank as well.

sentences.zh: 陝西五路師還，受命撫犒士卒，以疾先還者不賜。

translations.literal: When the five Shaanxi circuits' armies returned, he was ordered to comfort and reward the troops; those who returned early due to illness were not given rewards.
translations.idiomatic: When the five Shaanxi frontier armies returned, he was ordered to comfort and reward the troops, but those who had come back early because of illness received nothing.

sentences.zh: 惟簡心知其不便，至慶州，疏言：“士卒不幸，以將臣上違聖略，糧食不繼，逃生以歸，其情可貸。

translations.literal: Weijian knew in his heart this was unwise; reaching Qing prefecture, he memorialized: "The soldiers were unfortunate—because commanders disobeyed the sage strategy and supplies failed, they fled home to save their lives; their plight deserves leniency.
translations.idiomatic: Weijian saw the policy was wrong; at Qingzhou he memorialized: "The men were not to blame—officers had defied imperial strategy and left them without rations, so they fled home; that deserves mercy.

sentences.zh: 今同立庭中 而不預賜，恐患生倉卒。”

translations.literal: Now they stand together in the courtyard yet are not given rewards in advance—I fear trouble may arise suddenly."
translations.idiomatic: If they stand in the same courtyard yet the early returners are denied rewards, sudden unrest may follow."

sentences.zh: 帝用其言，均予之。

translations.literal: The Emperor adopted his advice and gave rewards equally to all.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his view and paid every man alike.

sentences.zh: 又使案閱河北保甲，振濟京西水災，參定諸陵薦獻。

translations.literal: He was again sent to review Hebei militia registers, relieve flood victims in western capital circuits, and help fix offerings at the imperial tombs.
translations.idiomatic: He was also ordered to inspect Hebei militia rolls, aid flood victims in the western capital region, and regulate offerings at the imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 既而為言者所劾，擯不用。

translations.literal: Before long he was impeached by critics and pushed aside from office.
translations.idiomatic: Critics soon impeached him and he was cast out of favor.

sentences.zh: 哲宗在藩時，惟簡奔奏服勤，及親 政，召至左右。

translations.literal: When Zhezong was still heir apparent, Weijian hurried in attendance with devoted service; when he took the throne personally, Weijian was summoned to his side.
translations.idiomatic: While Zhezong was still heir, Weijian had served him diligently; at his accession he was called back to the inner circle.

sentences.zh: 以內侍押班卒，贈昭化軍留後。

translations.literal: He died while Inner Attendant Service escort leader and was posthumously made deputy commissioner of the Zhaohua Army.
translations.idiomatic: He died as chief escort of the Inner Attendant Service and was posthumously honored as deputy commissioner of the Zhaohua Army.
